items.title: Vanguard, others organise Lagos gov debate: Our plans for housing, traffic, others — APC, ADC, NDC, PDP candidates
items.description: By Efe Onodjae LAGOS — THE Lagos State governorship candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Dr Obafemi Hamzat; African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty and Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, unveiled their development plans for housing, traffic congestion, transportation, security and infrastructure if elected in 2027. Read Also: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal They presented their credentials, policy proposals and vision for the state ahead of the governorship election. The candidates spoke at a debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, which comprises Vanguard Newspaper, Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper and The Cable. During the debate, the candidates outlined different approaches to addressing the developmental challenges facing Lagos. On the developmental challenges facing the state, the APC candidate, Dr Hamzat, emphasised continuity and expansion of existing infrastructure, while the ADC candidate, Mr Rhodes-Vivour, called for a departure from what he described as two decades of bad governance. In his remarks, the NDC candidate, Mr Doherty, questioned the political interests surrounding the state’s public transportation system, alleging that the failure to modernise the sector was deliberate. Taming traffic in Lagos On traffic congestion, Doherty alleged that the persistent gridlock in Lagos was being sustained by vested interests benefiting from the existing chaotic public transportation system. He argued that the state’s traffic problems were not simply the result of inadequate infrastructure but also reflected poor management of existing roads and the failure to modernise public transportation. The NDC candidate also alluded to the informal transport network popularly associated with agberos, arguing that the interests surrounding the system had made its modernisation politically difficult. He said: “Lagos continues to rely on dilapidated commercial buses operating chaotically, contributing to gridlock and making commuting difficult for residents. “Our public transportation system is not modernised. Thousands of rickety buses are moving around. We must ask ourselves: are these what our people deserve? Why has it taken so long to modernise public transportation? “In my opinion, the lack of modern transportation is not by accident. There are vested interests in operating the bus system the way it is. Many of us understand the agbero system; there is an ecosystem around it, and there is no political will to deal with that problem.” “We would modernise public transportation because we would be elected by the people and not by the agbero network,” he added. Hamzat, on his part, proposed expanding the state’s Bus Rapid Transit, BRT, system from about 1,000 buses to 4,000, with a target of transporting one million passengers daily. “The plan would involve deploying Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and creating dedicated BRT corridors across major routes. Integrated transportation system linking road, rail and water networks, saying the approach “would provide commuters with alternative means of movement and reduce pressure on major roads.” Housing, urban devt On housing, the ADC candidate, Mr Rhodes-Vivour, proposed delivering 100,000 housing units within his first four years in office through a combination of luxury taxation to fund social housing, development of the eastern foreshore and intergenerational areas, and decentralisation of development across the state. He argued that Lagos required an integrated approach to urban development, noting that housing, waste management, transportation, healthcare, education and urban planning were interconnected. Hamzat, on his part, said the Lagos State government had delivered 18,000 housing units in the last eight years, adding that plans were underway to expand access to affordable homes through mortgage financing. He said: “The proposed mortgage arrangement would allow prospective homeowners to make an initial payment of between 10 and 25 per cent and spread the balance over an extended period.” Meanwhile, the PDP candidate, Mr Doherty, proposed that the Lagos State Government should become a major property developer and build houses which residents could rent directly from the government. He said: “There is no landlord, and there is no government that can control a landlord. What we are going to do is very simple. We are going to rent those houses ourselves, and then you can come and rent from us if you want to. If they cannot compete with the landlords, then let us forget it.” Governance, experience Presenting his credentials, Hamzat described the debate as a job interview, saying his professional background and experience in public service had prepared him for the responsibility of governing Lagos. He said: “I take tonight (yesterday night) as a job interview. The first question you ask anybody who wants this type of responsibility is, what have you done to prepare for this job?” On his governing philosophy, he identified respect for citizens, hard work and truthfulness as the principles that would guide his administration. Unveiling his development blueprint, tagged ‘Jacob’s Promise,’ Hamzat said it was built around seven pillars, seven broad areas of action and 100 pledges. He urged voters to assess candidates based on the substance of their plans and the work behind their promises rather than political announcements. Similarly, Rhodes-Vivour said Lagos needs a departure from what he described as “two decades of bad governance,” insisting that the state must work for all residents rather than a privileged few. He said his political activism and manifesto had consistently prioritised the interests of ordinary people. Lagos economy Addressing the economic situation, Hamzat said Nigeria was undergoing a financial corrective phase, noting that the situation had made transportation, housing and food affordability major concerns for residents. He said although the Lagos State government had limited control over some economic variables, it could intervene in critical sectors such as housing, agriculture and transportation to ease the burden on residents. He said the completion and expansion of the Blue and Red rail lines, alongside investments in water transportation, would help move more commuters and reduce pressure on the roads. Hamzat added that the state’s development plans included procuring between 3,000 and 4,000 CNG buses to improve public transportation. In his presentation, the PDP candidate, Mr Deji Doherty, promised to abolish taxes imposed on teachers and doctors if elected governor in 2027. Unveiling his campaign agenda tagged ‘Awaken Lagos’, the PDP candidate said his administration would prioritise the welfare of professionals in the education and health sectors by granting them tax relief. He said: “I am cancelling teachers’ tax. Doctors, I am cancelling their tax. My campaign is Awaken Lagos.” Vanguard News The post Vanguard, others organise Lagos gov debate: Our plans for housing, traffic, others — APC, ADC, NDC, PDP candidates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Los sindicatos se preparan para un seguimiento “desigual” de la huelga por territorios, sectores y edades
items.description: El éxito y el fracaso siempre son cuestión de expectativas. En una huelga general, por definición, el éxito es que pare la actividad económica y el fracaso, que prosiga como si nada. Y atendiendo a las expectativas que transmiten más de una docena de sindicalistas con puestos de responsabilidad y consultados para este texto, y que hablan sin cortapisas en condición de anonimato, la huelga general del 11 de noviembre no parece en disposición de parar España, no como lo consiguieron los grandes paros del pasado. Pero, de darse ese escenario, no creen que ello deba identificarse como un pinchazo de esta “huelga rara”, como la definen algunas de las fuentes consultadas. No si la imagen de la tarde es tan potente que consiguen cambiar la conciencia del país en materia de vivienda, en línea con el impacto que consiguieron las marchas feministas del 8 de marzo de 2018 . Seguir leyendo Organización desde abajo Otras personas también están construyendo la huelga general desde sus barrios, como el getafense Sergio Jaramillo. Este arquitecto de 35 años es uno de los participantes en el comité de huelga de este municipio madrileño, donde se reúnen desde hace semanas y cooperan unitariamente organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas. “Hay dos equipos de trabajo. Uno orientado a la preparación de la huelga y otro a la difusión”, explica. “Está viniendo mucha gente, sobre todo gente joven con muchas ganas, incluso que no pertenece a ninguna organización pero quiere poner de su parte porque están muy cansados con la situación actual”, añade Jaramillo. “Habrá piquetes, pero como comprenderás no te voy a decir dónde”. Fuentes de los sindicatos clásicos y de los más pequeños subrayan que la organización de las manifestaciones de la tarde empezó con cierta tensión entre las partes, pero que se han acercado posturas con el paso de las semanas y que ahora hay más alineación de la esperada. A ambos lados subrayan la intermediación y el protagonismo del Sindicato de Inquilinas como una clave que, por lo general, ha operado a favor. En la gran mayoría de las ciudades las movilizaciones unirán a casi todo el movimiento a favor de la huelga. En Madrid y Barcelona CC OO y UGT van de la mano del Sindicato de Inquilinas y de CGT, CNT y la mayoría de sindicatos pequeños, escenario que se repite en muchas otras capitales. Y donde las Inquilinas no tienen presencia, también impera el entendimiento entre los sindicatos anarquistas y los mayoritarios. Sin embargo, el acuerdo no ha fructificado en Zaragoza , donde las Inquilinas marchan con los sindicatos alternativos, independientemente de la protesta de CC OO y UGT. Tampoco hay entendimiento entre los sindicatos pequeños y los grandes en Granada, en Valladolid y en Pamplona. Cabe precisar que en las dos grandes ciudades de España, aunque las Inquilinas se han coordinado con CC OO, UGT, CGT y CNT, la Coordinadora Juvenil Socialista (CJS) lidera su propia convocatoria en Madrid y Barcelona. En la capital convocan a las 17.00 en Atocha, una hora antes que la convocatoria mayoritaria, junto a CO.BAS y otros sindicatos menores. La CJS, una de las organizaciones clave de la acampada de Sol, es la voz que más consistentemente está siendo crítica con los sindicatos mayoritarios en los últimos días. Esa posición tan agresiva contra CC OO y UGT a las puertas de la huelga general ha sido rebatida públicamente incluso por miembros importantes de la Confederación de Sindicatos de Inquilinas. Otro conato de división que muestra la falta de entendimiento en algunos comités de huelga y en ciertos espacios organizativos es el de la Mesa Sindical de Madrid (compuesta por representantes madrileños de ASC, CGT, CNT Madrid Comarcal Sur, Co.bas, MATS, Plataforma Sindical EMT y Solidaridad Obrera), que acusan a las direcciones madrileñas de CC OO y UGT en una carta pública de “frenar la preparación de la huelga” en algunas empresas. “No estamos dispuestos a convertir esta convocatoria de huelga general en una precampaña para ningún partido”, añade ese comunicado. Voces de CC OO y UGT vienen restando importancia a estos pronunciamientos, que no ven alineados con el tono general de la mayoría del sindicalismo alternativo de cara al 11-N. Y subrayan que la sintonía con el Sindicato de Inquilinas está siendo la norma. A la vez, sostienen que justo en busca de esa unidad han rebajado el protagonismo que suelen tener en las manifestaciones asociadas a una huelga general, que comparten más espacio del que correspondería por su peso en los centros de trabajo. “Es una huelga diferente en todos los sentidos. No podemos ignorar el protagonismo del Sindicato de Inquilinas y la imagen de todos juntos es muy positiva, aunque sea a costa de ceder más espacio del habitual”, agrega un responsable de uno de estos sindicatos.

items.title: Más de la mitad de la oferta de alquiler de vivienda es de habitaciones y de temporada
items.description: Los alquileres de temporada y por habitaciones superaban a los residenciales en uno de los principales portales inmobiliarios antes de la aprobación del decreto de vivienda de octubre , que endurece los supuestos en los que pueden celebrarse. Entre marzo y septiembre de este año, en los seis meses previos a la entrada en vigor del nuevo marco normativo, el 55,8% de los anuncios publicados en las capitales españolas correspondieron a alguna de estas dos modalidades, frente al 44,2% de viviendas ofertadas para residencia habitual, según un estudio elaborado por el Ministerio de Consumo bajo la coordinación del investigador experto en vivienda Javier Gil, del Instituto de Filosofía del Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (IFS-CSIC). Los datos apuntan en la misma dirección que defiende el departamento que dirige Pablo Bustinduy: el mercado de arrendamientos viene desplazándose en los últimos años hacia fórmulas menos estables y con menores garantías para el inquilino. items.title: Cómo la televisión española se convirtió en una tertulia política infinita
items.description: En 1996, en las tardes de TVE se emitía una telenovela y en las de Antena 3 Los Simpson . Diez años después, fue el tiempo de los talk shows , la prensa del corazón y los primeros grandes formatos de telerrealidad. En 2016, buena parte del prime time seguía girando en torno a lo familiar, lo cultural o la comedia. Ahora, en 2026, la política lo impregna casi todo: las cadenas generalistas encadenan tertulias por la mañana, por la tarde y, en muchos casos, también por la noche. Acaba de nacer de hecho La Séptima , una cadena que basa su programación en la actualidad. Y este mismo lunes, el líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, es el invitado en La Revuelta , el programa de entretenimiento estrella de La 1. ¿Cómo se ha producido esa transformación? ¿Qué efectos tiene sobre el ánimo de los espectadores y sobre la polarización ciudadana? ¿Es posible hacer televisión política sin contribuir al ruido? items.title: A shifting cycle
items.description: PAKISTAN’S 2024 election results marked the end of a political cycle that began in the early 2000s. Less often noted is that this cycle expired at roughly the same moment as the global order which framed it. Signs of political and cultural realignment are now fully emergent, and their trajectory passes through events of the past 25 years — the ‘war on terror’ and its effects on Muslim societies, the financial crisis alongside growth in Asian economies, and increased migration to Western countries. The Pakistani domestic cycle is best characterised as an unsuccessful attempt to achieve a political settlement, under the garb of federalised (and electoral) constitutional rule. Its participants were the traditional parties PML-N and PPP, and their core constituents, sections of liberal civil society and private news media, and some segments of the judiciary. Its opposition came from entities excluded from or antagonised by that brief lived system of patronage: the PTI, the upwardly mobile urban classes, and the military establishment and its aligned factions among the media. The latter coalition won out over the last 10 years. In winning, it stumbled upon its own internal contradictions, which are now playing out as the present crisis. This cycle, however, was always nested inside something larger. Its vocabulary of rights, its civil society, and much of its international support came from a global dispensation; NGO work here was intellectually and financially sustained by Western aid largesse in the context of the war on terror. Once the external scaffolding weakened, the undoing at home proved swift. That scaffolding is what we commonly dub the neoliberal world order. Characterised by deregulation in markets, and trade and financial liberalisation, these prescriptions were macroeconomic orthodoxy for nearly four decades. They represented the response of the capitalist class to the stagflation crisis of the 1970s in Western economies, dismantling the political power of labour by making offshoring easier, and restoring the power of capital through financialisation. The recipe would remain incomplete without access to new labour, product, and capital markets, which is why it came packaged as IMF-run ‘structural adjustment’ for countries in the Global South. The Pakistani domestic cycle is best characterised as an unsuccessful attempt to achieve a political settlement. What did these four decades of liberalisation deliver? Growth for some countries (East Asia, parts of Latin America), stagnation and deindustrialisation for most others, astronomical returns for owners of finance capital, and heightened inequality nearly everywhere. Since 2008, populations in the West have rightly soured on this misfiring orthodoxy, and that resentment has gradually made its way into how decision-makers think about their economies. Free markets are no longer considered orthodoxy (at least in rhetoric). The unravelling of the old order extends beyond economics. Liberal democracy was presented as a core value, supposedly maintained by the US globally. Its use as a cynical foreign policy stick had already made many in the world wary. Elsewhere, the appeal of some authoritarian systems is growing. Sociologist Cihan Tugal points to Turkiye under Erdogan and the AKP, which has used state welfare, economic intervention, and centralised politics to contain opposition over two decades. Key political and establishment figures in countries like Pakistan now routinely view limits on democracy as necessary for economic progress. Does this reordering then offer Pakistan an opening? Statist nationalists see the country’s expanded role in regional geopolitical affairs as both a vindication of its military-led governing structure and a route to its destined status as a regional power. On the face of it, both shifts work in the country’s favour. As a state with strong military capabilities, both nuclear and conventional, Pakistan can extract material concessions from regional powers looking for a security patron after the US winds down its position. And for a country long locked into IMF programmes , escaping some elements of neoliberal economic orthodoxy is a necessity. The real question is: can it? Here the answer goes back to how the global is refracted into the local via the domestic arrangements that actually exist on the ground. Can the rentier/ patronage economy be turned productive? Can those with outsized claims on the exchequer be reined in? The task rests with a state overwhelmed by a military-bureaucratic establishment that has turned its primary logic into one of extraction via authoritarian decree rather than service delivery. More importantly, this is a state of viceregal origin, incapable of the mass mobilisation and disciplining that engendered effective capacity in Korea or China. It is held together instead by the distribution of rents, internally to its cadres and kin, and externally to a narrow sliver of the population. The traditional parties that might have steered this moment have proven completely unable to do so. Their mode of politics rested on narrow patronage relations with socially dominant segments in Punjab and Sindh, and in exchange for temporary respite they outsourced Fata, Balochistan, judicial independence, electoral competition, and even large parts of governance to the militarised logic of establishment control. Most of all, they have ignored the emergent reality of the upwardly mobile, digitally resourceful urban middle classes and inflation-weary masses, leaving the field wide open for multiple types of resentment. However, resentment on its own is insufficient to lead society anywhere. The arduous task for those still committed to broad-based material uplift lies in reworking the state into something attentive to the collective good and capable of mobilising society for it. This is not a reworking that will be handed to progressives with any ease. In fact, in the absence of viable progressive movements to project some notion of universal justice, the militarisation of the region and the turn to narrow, sectional resentment is a recipe for further marginalisation of the already vulnerable. The writer teaches politics and sociology at Lums. X: @umairjav Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Media owners must invest in training, safety and fair remuneration – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Felix Kwake Ofosu, Minister in charge of Government Communications, has urged media owners and stakeholders to invest in professional training, improve working conditions, and ensure journalists’ safety as they perform their duties. Speaking at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra, he said journalists’ safety should be taken seriously, and no journalist should be assaulted, threatened, or unlawfully detained for undertaking a legitimate professional assignment. “Allegations of attacks, including those involving security personnel, must be investigated and accountability must follow where wrongdoing is established,” he noted. Mr Ofosu highlighted journalism’s contribution to national development and democracy, stressing that every institution committed to the rule of law should protect journalists. He expressed the government’s commitment to protecting media freedom and urged the media to keep interrogating policies and ensure officials remain answerable to the people. “We do not expect favourable headlines as a condition for engagement, nor do we expect journalists to surrender their editorial independence in the name of partnership.” “A government that is confident in its democratic credentials must be prepared to answer difficult questions and accept legitimate criticism,” he noted. The Minister emphasised the dangers of hate speech on digital platforms, which stakeholders in the industry and beyond must confront without compromising the right to free speech. He said there must be a clear distinction between criminal conduct and free speech, adding that combating hate speech must not justify suppressing critical journalism or unpopular opinions. “Democracy thrives on disagreement and what it cannot accommodate is the deliberate incitement of hatred, violence and intolerance…our words in support of free speech must not ring hollow,” he said. Mr Ofosu commended Ghana’s 39th ranking on the 2026 Press Freedom Index, urging stakeholders to continue promoting press freedom. “The true measure of press freedom is whether a journalist can investigate wrongdoing without intimidation, report on public affairs without fear and express an independent editorial opinion without unlawful retaliation.” “The day journalists stop asking difficult questions should be the day those in government begin to worry…a free media is not a threat to responsible government but its strongest safeguard…” he said. He said the government will continue to maintain cordial relationships with the media and help unravel the circumstances surrounding the murder of investigative journalist Ahmed Sualley. The ceremony, themed “30th GJA Media Awards: Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age,” celebrated the media’s contribution to Ghana’s democratic governance, national cohesion and socio-economic development, and renewed the call for responsible journalism, media freedom and professionalism in the digital era. It also recognised national personalities whose exceptional leadership and service had impacted Ghana’s democratic governance, public service, security, traditional leadership, entrepreneurship and socio-economic development Mr Alber Dwumfour, President of GJA, highlighted the evolving threats against journalists and called for a dedicated police focal point for journalist safety and complaints. He said the Association will continue to protect journalists’ interests and support legislation to improve practitioners’ working conditions and welfare.

items.title: Nvidia probes whether CEO Huang was target of foreign spying as he admits affair
items.description: Nvidia said on Monday its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Huang said in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and took “full responsibility” for his actions, while Nvidia said the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption. The developments are likely to pressure the chipmaker’s stock, which has already fallen sharply amid worries about the AI boom’s sustainability, and may also raise questions about Huang’s future at the helm of the company he co-founded, analysts said. The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia, over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China. “The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation,” Nvidia said. The company said on Sunday that while its board had no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine all available information. The board has confidence in the CEO and his leadership team, Nvidia said, adding that Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had not spoken to Huang about the allegations, but called him a fine person. “I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job,” he added. When asked if he believed he should have acted on intelligence when he was briefed about it, Trump said: “No, I don’t think so. I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.” The New York Times had reported that Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to do anything with the information. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on Huang when asked by reporters earlier in the evening. Chinas foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Huang said on Sunday that he was “committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security.” Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment outside business hours. Piling pressure on Nvidia The investigation adds to pressure on Nvidia at a time investors are already pulling back amid uncertainty over the sustainability of the booming AI market that made the chipmaker one of the world’s most valuable companies. The $4.5 trillion chipmaker’s shares have given up all their gains this year amid a broader tech market rout triggered by worries over the pace of AI spending. Huang, who has led Nvidia for more than three decades, has been central to its rise to become a dominant supplier of AI chips. “There is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the Board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally,” said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co. “This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock,” Ives said, adding that the news would also increase scrutiny about selling chips to China. Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife, saying, “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, Huang said: “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.” In late October, he had told Bloomberg News that his relationship and interactions with Alice Huang were related to Megaspeed and were “completely normal and not unusual”. Josh Gilbert, lead analyst at trading platform eToro, said Huang’s fingerprints were on every part of the company’s rise, so any doubt over his position would matter to shareholders. “While the investigation is likely to dent sentiment, it won’t alter anything long-term unless it leads to a change at the top, at which point it becomes a completely different ball game,” Gilbert added. Top Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives had already called on Huang to brief Congress this month about the New York Times report. The report raises “significant national security concerns regarding (China’s) access to sensitive US technology and information,” the lawmakers said in a letter dated November 4. “It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk,” they added. US export controls since 2022 have sought to restrict China’s access to advanced Nvidia chips and the equipment needed to make them.

items.title: Mother of quadruplets appeals for support as cost of childcare mounts
items.description: A mother of four one-year-old boys at Gorm in the Ada East District has appealed for financial and material support as the rising cost of caring for the four children overwhelms the family’s limited resources. Madam Felicia Kisseh said the family struggled to provide food, diapers, and other essential supplies for the children, whose needs had placed considerable financial pressure on her and her husband. Madam Kisseh said the quadruplets were not their only children, as they also had an eight-year-old son whose needs they had to meet as well. In an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA), she noted that although individuals and organisations provided assistance after the quadruplets’ birth, the supplies and financial support ran out within six months. She said her husband, Mr John Felix Agbesi, a mason, could not earn enough to meet the family’s growing needs. Madam Kisseh, who formerly worked to support the household, said caring for the four boys day and night made it difficult for her to return to work. She estimated the family needed about GH¢2,600 monthly for two boxes of baby food, plus about GH¢500 for 50 nappies. She said the children also ate prepared meals, including rice mixed with boiled carrots and blended with banana and milk. The mother said the recurring cost of these essential items had made it increasingly difficult for the family to provide consistently for the children. “I don’t know how we are going to survive again because everything we hoped for is failing us. Some philanthropists assisted us when I gave birth to them, including the Member of Parliament, Nana Tea and a few others, but all the foodstuffs are finished,” she said. Madam Kisseh said the family continued to struggle with the expenses of raising four children of the same age, adding that, despite the challenges, her love for the boys remained unwavering. “I love my boys. Looking at them makes me feel fulfilled, but when they start crying from hunger, I become frustrated and confused. It overwhelms me,” she said. She appealed to philanthropists, charitable organisations, corporate institutions, and well-meaning individuals for food, baby supplies, and financial assistance to meet the children’s needs. She said any assistance would help ease the family’s financial burden and enable them to provide the children with the care and nourishment they needed. Individuals and organisations willing to assist the family may send contributions to her mobile money number, 0548912995, in the name of Kisseh Felicia.

items.title: INEC in Eye of the Storm: Electoral body battles to clean voters’ register – Investigation
items.description: By Jide Ajani There is perhaps no greater threat to electoral integrity than an unreliable Voters’ Register. Before the first ballot is cast or the first result announced, the credibility of an election is already being determined by the document that establishes who is entitled to vote. Read Also: * Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal The Voters’ Register is the foundation of the electoral process. It defines the electorate, determines the numerical strength of constituencies and provides the basis for accreditation and voting. It is, fundamentally, the official record of a people’s democratic membership. Yet, in Nigeria, its credibility remains a persistent source of anxiety. The historical paradox: have we really progressed? Nigeria has travelled a considerable distance from the largely manual registration arrangements of the 1950s to biometric registration, electronic databases and the deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). The 1959 general election, conducted under the Electoral Commission of Nigeria (ECN), had approximately nine million registered voters. Subsequent elections in 1964/65, 1979, 1983 and 1993 exposed different administrative and political challenges associated with voter registration. 4th Republic The Fourth Republic introduced more sophisticated systems, including permanent voter cards, biometric identification and mechanisms for detecting duplicate registrations. Yet technological advancement has not necessarily translated into greater electoral credibility. A bigger register is not automatically a better register. A digital register is not necessarily reliable, and biometric technology is not beyond manipulation. Consider the fluctuations in registration figures: 73.5 million in 2011, 67.4 million in 2015 and approximately 84 million in 2019. Such changes do not establish manipulation, since legitimate deletions and corrections occur The real test is fidelity: whether the names represent living, eligible citizens entitled to vote, or whether they are mere AI-generated entities. INEC and the collapse of public confidence An electoral commission’s credibility rests not merely on constitutional independence but on demonstrable impartiality, competence and transparency. Constitutional independence in itself does not guarantee operational independence when the personnel saddled with responsibilities decide to go rogue on the system. When public confidence in INEC declines, virtually every administrative decision becomes vulnerable to suspicion, from voter registration and PVC distribution to accreditation and results management. This is the distinction between administrative validity and democratic legitimacy. The former concerns compliance with prescribed procedures; the latter concerns whether citizens believe those procedures have produced a trustworthy outcome. The European Union Election Observation Mission’s final report on the 2023 elections identified shortcomings in electoral administration that undermined public confidence. It also recommended an independent external audit of the Voters’ Register, including physical data checks and an assessment of biometric data quality. This is significant. Concerns about the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral database extend beyond opposition-party allegations. The law is clear: why must the register be open to the people? Section 19 of the Electoral Act provides for public display and scrutiny of the Voters’ Register. INEC is required to designate a seven-day period, not later than 90 days before a general election, for displaying the register at Registration Areas and publishing it on its official website or another designated website. The law also provides for claims and objections concerning improperly included or omitted names. Failure by an INEC official to display or publish the register constitutes an offence under Section 19(5). Public inspection allows citizens to identify omissions, questionable entries and incorrect transfers. It also enables political parties, civil society organisations and election observers to scrutinise the database before election day. This is democratic quality control, not an administrative favour. A register that is inaccessible, inadequately publicised or concealed behind bureaucratic obstacles defeats the purpose of the law. INEC cannot be the sole custodian, examiner and final judge of its own database. An INEC source disclosed to Vanguard that the display of the register at wards and online has tremendously helped the commission to identify duplications and other impurities in the register. According to the source, “hundreds of thousands of claims and objections have so far been received by the commission and more are still being expected. You will recall that when the present leadership of the commission took over, we wanted to carry out a revalidation exercise. That exercise would have helped to clean the register in a more seamless manner. But the public outcry against the revalidation forced the hands of commission to abandon the idea. Mind you, we have carried out three phases of continuous voter registration” Vanguard also learnt that the commission is presently on a zonal review of the exercise and has committed to presenting a clean register by December 15, 2026. The dangerous politics of padding the register In a political environment where electoral strength is often measured numerically, the temptation to inflate registration figures is obvious. Padding may involve duplicate identities, ineligible persons, deceased registrants, fictitious entries or manipulated personal information. Nigeria’s biometric system was designed partly to prevent such abuses. Fingerprints and facial recognition can help identify duplicate records, but their effectiveness depends on data quality, institutional oversight and the integrity of officials operating the system. The register must therefore be protected against both external manipulation and insider misconduct through access controls, audit trails, independent verification and meaningful sanctions. That is what INEC claims it is doing. The emergence of artificial intelligence introduces another troubling dimension. Just last month, (October 2026), concerns emerged over suspected AI-generated photographs, duplicate records and questionable entries in Nigeria’s preliminary Voters’ Register. INEC acknowledged investigating the irregularities, while its Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, attributed some questionable records to alleged misconduct by registration officers with access to the platform. Meanwhile, INEC has refused to release the names of those officials, further poisoning an already polluted space AI can generate convincing synthetic facial images and identity-related material. However, a suspicious photograph does not automatically establish that a fictitious person has been registered. Each affected identity must be independently investigated. INEC must explain how such records entered the database, their number, whether they have been removed and what safeguards have been introduced to prevent recurrence. A national electoral database cannot depend on the assumption that everyone with access to it will act honestly. It must be designed to detect dishonesty. Pvc distribution: When registration does not translate into voting Registration means little if citizens cannot exercise the rights it confers. INEC’s figures for the 2023 general election showed that, of 93,469,008 registered voters, 87,209,007 had collected their PVCs as at February 5, 2023. More than six million registered voters had not collected their cards. This raises questions about administrative inefficiency, notification, relocation and access to collection centres. The disconnect between registration and participation is equally troubling. This discrepancy does not prove fraud. This discrepancy does not prove fraud. Apathy, insecurity and logistical challenges also affect participation. Nevertheless, it reinforces the need for a register that accurately reflects the eligible electorate and a system that enables citizens to vote. Other structural weaknesses These are not peripheral administrative issues. A defective register also creates opportunities for electoral litigation, as candidates, parties, and voters may challenge questionable entries, omissions, and accreditation figures. An unreliable register does not automatically invalidate an election, but it introduces uncertainty into every subsequent stage of the process. What INEC must do to restore fidelity INEC should commission an independent audit of the national register, examining duplicate identities, biometric inconsistencies, deceased registrants, underage entries, and questionable photographs. It must enforce Section 19 of the Electoral Act, ensure meaningful public inspection, and provide appropriately protected, searchable polling-unit-level information. It must remove verified death records, strengthen voter-transfer procedures, introduce stricter database access controls, and publish periodic explanations of additions, deletions, and corrections. PVC collection must become more accessible, while officials responsible for deliberate manipulation must face meaningful accountability. Transparency must be an operational principle, not a public-relations exercise. Democracy begins before the ballot is cast Nigeria’s electoral credibility cannot be separated from the 1950s and today’s sophisticated biometric systems should have produced an electoral environment in which the identity and eligibility of voters are beyond reasonable suspicion. That this remains a subject of national controversy is a sobering indictment of past electoral administrations. In a democracy, the register belongs, in the fullest sense, to the Nigerian people whose voting rights it records. Nigeria does not necessarily need a bigger Voters’ Register. Ultimately, a free, fair, and credible election does not begin on election morning. It begins much earlier, with the painstaking work of establishing who is entitled to vote. The integrity of the ballot is inseparable from the integrity of the register. Where the foundation is uncertain, the legitimacy of the electoral outcome will always remain vulnerable – as it has always been. items.title: Journalists are not enemies of the state, security institutions – Dwumfour
items.description: Albert Kwabena Dwumfour, President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), has called for justice for media practitioners attacked or assaulted in the line of duty. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra on Saturday, he said the Association had recorded more than 50 incidents involving journalists who were attacked, arrested or threatened between 2022 and 2026. He called for transparent investigations and timely prosecution of culpable perpetrators, particularly in cases involving security personnel. “Journalists are not enemies of the state or security institutions; they are partners in national development. An attack on journalists is an attack on press freedom, our democracy and the public’s right to information,” he said. Mr Dwumfour highlighted the evolving threats facing media personnel and called for a dedicated police focal point to handle journalist safety and related complaints. He said the Association would continue to protect journalists’ interests and support legislation to improve their working conditions and welfare. “Improving journalists’ welfare is an investment in media independence, professional integrity and the quality of our democracy,” he said. The GJA President said journalists could not be expected to deliver courageous, independent and ethical journalism without due consideration for the economic circumstances under which they worked. “Those who dedicate their lives to informing society, holding power accountable and defending the public interest deserve decent working conditions and a dignified standard of living,” he added. Mr Dwumfour urged media practitioners to operate within the industry’s regulatory frameworks, stressing that state officials should enforce and ensure compliance with fairness, professionalism, and sensitivity to the human and economic consequences. “The fact that a media organisation may have breached a regulatory requirement should not automatically make the livelihoods of its workers collateral damage,” he said. He commended the award winners and thanked President John Dramani Mahama for supporting initiatives that promoted press freedom. Mr Felix Fosu Kwakye, Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, urged media owners and stakeholders to invest in professional training, improve working conditions, and ensure journalists’ safety as they discharge their duties. The ceremony, held on the theme: “30th GJA Media Awards: Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age,” recognised the media’s contribution to Ghana’s democratic governance, national cohesion and socio-economic development. It also renewed calls for responsible journalism, media freedom and professionalism in the digital era. The event also recognised national personalities whose exceptional leadership and service have contributed to Ghana’s democratic governance, public service, security, traditional leadership, entrepreneurship, and socio-economic development. Thirty-six journalists received awards across categories, including three from the Ghana News Agency.

items.title: El bloque de la derecha mantiene su ventaja pero el PSOE se acerca al PP
items.description: A tres semanas para que se abran las urnas en España, la ventaja del bloque de la derecha se muestra inalterable. La suma del PP, Vox y UPN en las elecciones generales del próximo día 29 reuniría la mitad de los votos emitidos y rebasaría los 190 escaños, más de 15 por encima de la mayoría absoluta del Congreso, según la última encuesta de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER. La mayor incertidumbre en estos momentos reside en quién será el más votado de entre los dos grandes partidos, ya que la diferencia entre PP y PSOE se ha acortado a dos puntos, dentro del margen de error del sondeo. Los socialistas experimentan un importante avance, pese a la catástrofe ferroviaria de Urda , mientras los grupos a su izquierda se sitúan bajo mínimos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La huelga divide a los españoles y más de la mitad rechaza las acampadas
items.description: La huelga general convocada por los sindicatos para el próximo miércoles día 11, con la vivienda como reivindicación principal, divide casi en dos mitades a los españoles. La apoyan un 46,3% y la rechazan algunos más, el 48,8%, según una encuesta de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER. La posición crítica con esos movimientos sociales crece un poco más en el caso de las acampadas, que las reprueban un 53% de los encuestados. Las medidas y decretos aprobados por el Gobierno para intentar atajar la carestía de la vivienda —el último paquete será probablemente aprobado este jueves por la Diputación Permanente del Congreso— despiertan escaso entusiasmo: apenas uno de cada cuatro entrevistados valoran su eficacia. Los microdatos de la encuesta, que también incluyen intención de voto, pueden consultarse en las webs de ambos medios . Seguir leyendo

items.title: El PP ampliará hasta los 50 años de edad el aval público para pagar la entrada de una casa
items.description: Con la edad de emancipación superior a los 30 años, una de las más altas de la Unión Europea , el Partido Popular propone ampliar la franja de edad para poder acceder al aval público para comprar una vivienda, desde los 35 años actuales hasta los 40, con la posibilidad de ampliarlo incluso hasta los 50 años. Así figura en su programa electoral para las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, al que ha tenido acceso en esa parte EL PAÍS. Los populares plantean también una rebaja del IVA para la compra de la primera vivienda del 10% al 4% para menores de 40 años, y permitirán que este impuesto se pague de forma fraccionada al ritmo de la hipoteca. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los helicópteros pioneros que salvaron vidas en el accidente de Urda: “Perdimos la cuenta de la gente a la que llegamos a atender”
items.description: Les llaman Los Gigantes, por los molinos de viento que hizo inmortales Miguel de Cervantes y por la misión quijotesca que libran salvando vidas a diario en las distancias infinitas de Castilla-La Mancha, la tercera comunidad más extensa de España. Muchas veces en medio de la nada, como en el accidente ferroviario de Urda . La capacidad de los servicios de emergencia de la Junta para hacer transfusiones de sangre en sus cuatro helicópteros sanitarios pudo evitar que la cifra de 69 fallecidos por la colisión del AVE con el Iryo fuese mayor. De los 110 heridos que fueron hospitalizados en seis hospitales de la región, solo falleció una persona. “Se hicieron transfusiones sobre el terreno a ocho pacientes. Les ganamos tiempo. Cada minuto que se retrasa la transfusión a un paciente que la necesita aumenta un 5% las posibilidades de que fallezca. Muy probablemente alguno lo hubiera hecho”, explica Alberto López, de 48 años y director de la Gerencia de Urgencias, Emergencias y Transporte Sanitario del Servicio de Salud de Castilla-La Mancha (Sescam). Seguir leyendo

items.title: Albares: “La comunidad iberoamericana está más polarizada que nunca”
items.description: Es viernes, jornada de resaca tras la Cumbre Iberoamericana de Madrid , cuando el ministro de Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, recibe a EL PAÍS para esta entrevista en el Palacio de Viana, una de las sedes de su ministerio. Defiende los resultados, a pesar de las diferencias en la comunidad iberoamericana: “Está más polarizada que nunca. El reto de conseguir ese consenso era mayor”. Y ve posibilidades de una victoria progresista el 29-N: “Esa ola que arranca en Brasil, sigue en Estados Unidos, va a seguir aquí en España”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Valdano: “El portero Owono es la segunda víctima de un accidente”
items.description: Asegura Jorge Valdano (Las Parejas, Santa Fe, Argentina, 71 años) que no es “nostálgico” y la frase tiene su aquel viniendo de alguien que fue campeón del mundo y que vio en primera fila el gol del siglo pasado. Tampoco parece haber guardado sitio para el rencor pese a los rejonazos en su etapa como directivo del Real Madrid. La voz serena y cultivada del fútbol asiste horrorizada al contagio de lo peor de su disciplina a la política: la hipérbole. En el país que le vio nacer y también en el que vive desde 1975. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La revuelta con el público de ‘La revuelta’: qué se juega Broncano frente a Abascal
items.description: “Abascal va a venir, eh. Es un jugón”, le advirtió Rufián a Broncano durante su visita a La revuelta . Se ve que tiene dotes adivinatorias o que algo sabe de su compañero de hemiciclo. Sea porque tiende a Bruja Lola o a Iván Redondo, el catalán no se equivocó. Este lunes Santiago Abascal , líder de Vox, capo de los que amenazan con llegar al a corporación pública con la motosierra encendida, será entrevistado en uno de los programas más denostados por la ultraderecha. “Nunca pensé que diría esto... pero en La revuelta , el lunes, Santiago Abascal ”, anunció la semana pasada un atribulado Broncano. El público, elemento imprescindible del formato, abucheó. Algo esperable en un espacio en el que los asistentes a las grabaciones jalean artículos de la Constitución sobre el derecho a la vivienda. Vox, temiendo una grada más hostil que las del Galatasaray, ha dicho que no quieren ese público, que le pongan otro. ¿Lo han dicho? Ha sido la comidilla desde que se anunció la visita. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Radiografía del Robe más desconocido: la primera canción que escribió se llamó ‘Cepillo de dientes’
items.description: La primera canción que escribió Roberto Iniesta llevaba por título uno tan poco poético como Cepillo de dientes . Era 1986 y el extremeño contaba 24 años. La letra dice así: “Casi prefiero quedarme ciego, casi prefiero quedarme cojo, casi prefiero quedarme sordo, casi prefiero quedarme mudo. / Has usado mi cepillo de dientes, lo has usado y me mientes, has usado mi cepillo de dientes, lo has usado y te voy a matar. / Has usado mi cepillo de dientes y no te lo voy a perdonar”. Lo desvela Paco Dóniga, bajista de Dosis Letal, la primera formación en la que militó Robe, en un documental de tres horas y media titulado Plasencia y Robe. Se trata del capítulo número 64 de La historia de Extremoduro, un hercúleo trabajo que está llevando a cabo Juan Carlos Ramos (Plasencia, 52 años), periodista y apasionado de la obra del autor de Se nos lleva el aire . Seguir leyendo

items.description: ¿Quién dice Texas y quién dice Tejas? ¿Quién los escribe cómo? Tejas fue durante siglos Tejas, pero ahora lleva años siendo Texas porque el inglés sabe infiltrarse de todas las maneras. En Tejas, con sudor y lágrimas y balas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La incógnita de Eisenkot en política exterior: pragmático, pero contrario a un Estado palestino
items.description: Gadi Eisenkot, el exjefe del ejército israelí que ha recibido este domingo el encargo presidencial de formar Gobierno, centra su discurso tanto en temas internos ( responsabilidad política por el ataque de Hamás , alistamiento de los ultraortodoxos, reparación institucional...) como en liderar la alternativa a Benjamín Netanyahu. Pero solo ha esbozado aquello por lo que justamente el mundo mira atento si logrará ser el próximo primer ministro de Israel: ¿Cómo pretende actuar en Irán, Gaza , Líbano o Siria? ¿Y con los palestinos? Seguir leyendo

items.title: La moral decae, pero Kiev se niega a bajar la persiana
items.description: La escena se repite en las calles de Kiev. Cada local, si no la mayoría, tiene un generador eléctrico en la puerta. Cuando están todos prendidos, puede llegar a ser una tortura; el ruido taladra hasta lo más profundo del cerebro. Pero es el precio que los habitantes de la capital ucrania tienen que pagar para seguir haciendo una vida medianamente normal en medio de los cortes de electricidad que ya se extienden hasta 17 horas al día y justo antes de empezar un invierno que, prevén, será el más duro desde el comienzo de la invasión a gran escala en 2022. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Kim Jong-un aprovecha la guerra de Ucrania para impulsar el poder militar de Corea del Norte
items.description: La actividad militar en Corea del Norte ha sido especialmente intensa en las últimas semanas. Los medios estatales han mostrado a su líder supremo, Kim Jong-un , volcado en la modernización del ejército: ha recorrido exposiciones de armamento , supervisado demostraciones con fuego real y exigido a sus científicos avances en el uso militar de la inteligencia artificial y el desarrollo de drones. Entretanto, Pyongyang ha realizado pruebas de proyectiles que presenta como hipersónicos, lanzamientos de misiles de crucero desde submarinos, pruebas con drones y ensayos de municiones de racimo. En paralelo, continúan las obras de fortificación de la frontera con Corea del Sur, que alimentan la tensión en la península , mientras Kim Yo-jong, la poderosa hermana del máximo dirigente, acompaña de amenazas ese despliegue . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ayuso baja el tono en precampaña: “El protagonista ahora es Feijóo”
items.description: Isabel Díaz Ayuso alcanzó un momento de máxima expansión una noche de principios de octubre. Apareció en el programa de televisión Horizonte , donde la pareja de presentadores, los periodistas y ufólogos Iker Jiménez y Carmen Porter, la entrevistaron durante algo más de una hora. Estuvo extraordinariamente locuaz y lucía radiante cuando la cámara se detenía en ella y cerraba el plano. Se notaba que se sentía cómoda —no por nada se trata de uno de sus shows favoritos—. Ayuso describió, sin que nadie la interrumpiera, una España ruinosa, gobernada por un tirano y confeccionada por familias al borde de la ruptura. Por momentos, Ayuso pareció eufórica. Cuando se marchó del plató, unos tertulianos se incorporaron a la mesa y celebraron la intervención de la presidenta de Madrid. Horizonte barrió esa noche al resto de la parrilla y logró su récord histórico de audiencia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El mundo le toma el pulso a la lucha climática en la cumbre de Turquía con la crisis petrolera como aliada
items.description: Cuando se acerca cada final de año, el mundo le toma el pulso en las cumbres de la ONU a la lucha internacional contra el cambio climático, un problema que se intenta abordar desde el multilateralismo desde hace casi 35 años. En la conferencia del pasado año, celebrada en la ciudad brasileña de Belém , casi se pierde definitivamente al paciente y salta por los aires todo. Tras un durísimo enfrentamiento entre países, la cumbre se cerró sin ni siquiera poder hacer una referencia directa en los textos finales a la necesidad de dejar atrás los combustibles fósiles, que son los principales responsables del calentamiento global. Un año después, los cerca de 200 países que forman parte de estas negociaciones —que están obligados a decidir cada palabra por consenso, lo que hace que siempre se diluya la ambición— se reúnen a partir de este lunes en la ciudad turca de Antalya, en la COP31, sin casi expectativas sobre la posibilidad de avances. Seguir leyendo

items.title: COCOBOD relaunches free fertiliser distribution programme in Western North Region
items.description: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD has officially re-launched the Free Fertiliser Distribution Programme as part of the government’s commitment to support cocoa farmers to improve farm productivity. The initiative also sought to ease the financial burden of purchasing fertiliser and enhance farmers’ livelihoods. Speaking at the launch in Sefwi-Wiawso, Dr Randy Abbey, Chief Executive Officer, COCOBOD, directed CHED officials to use technology to register farmers, noting that the move would eliminate favouritism, cut out middlemen, and ensure fertilisers and other agro inputs reached cocoa farmers directly. He expressed concern about how cocoa swollen shoot disease negatively affected cocoa production in the Western North Region, reducing it from 340,000 metric tonnes annually to 140,000 metric tonnes. He assured that COCOBOD was aggressively galvanising massive capital injections from development banks and private sector partners to rehabilitate diseased farms and restore farmers’ livelihoods. The COCOBOD CEO further announced that the Board was working to kick-start the tertiary scholarship for cocoa farmers’ children starting in the 2027/2027 academic year. Dr Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo, COCOBOD Board Chairman, urged farmers to ensure they properly apply the fertilisers they receive to improve soil fertility and increase cocoa yields. He also cautioned against diverting the fertiliser, saying enhanced tracking technology had been deployed to monitor distribution from the warehouse to farms and ensure the intended beneficiaries received the inputs. Mr Wilbert Petty Brentum, the Western North Regional Minister, said COCOBOD’s decision to relaunch the programme in the region underscored the government’s continued commitment to revitalising the cocoa sector, improving productivity, and enhancing the livelihoods of cocoa farmers. He lauded farmers for demonstrating resilience and determination to sustain the cocoa industry despite the negative impacts of the cocoa swollen shoot and other diseases on farms. Mr Brentum further called for the privatisation of the rehabilitation programme in the region, saying the move would help provide the much-needed financial relief to farmers. Nana Ofori Ahenkan II, Chief of Bonzain and Acting President of the Wiawso Traditional Council, who chaired the programme, said cocoa farmers’ dedication over the years has significantly boosted Ghana’s cocoa production fortunes. He emphasised that the free fertiliser distribution would not only secure the future of Ghana's cocoa sector, but ultimately improve the livelihoods of cocoa farmers and their households. He urged cocoa farmers to take full advantage of the programme, use it for its intended purpose, and follow recommendations and application guidelines to achieve the best results. Some farmers in an interview with the Ghana News Agency, lauded the government and COCOBOD for the initiative, saying it would help improve yields. They also welcomed COCOBOD’s decision to begin scholarships for their children in the next academic year, saying it would ease their financial burden.

items.title: Yagbonwura calls for stronger collaboration among traditional authorities to promote peace
items.description: Yagbonwura Bii-Kunuto Jewu Soale I, King and Overlord of the Gonja Kingdom and President of the Savannah Regional House of Chiefs, has called for stronger collaboration among traditional authorities across the country to promote peace, good governance and community development. He said regular engagements among Traditional Councils and Regional Houses of Chiefs would provide opportunities for the sharing of experiences and the development of common solutions to challenges confronting communities. The Yagbonwura made the call when addressing the chiefs and people of Anlo as the Special Guest of Honour at the 64th edition of the Hogbetsotso Festival at Anloga in the Volta Region on Saturday. He said traditional authorities must also strengthen partnerships with Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) and other state institutions to promote development consultations, peacebuilding, environmental protection and community mobilisation. He, however, stressed that such collaboration must operate within the respective constitutional and legal mandates of the institutions. The Yagbonwura urged traditional leaders to rise above narrow interests and work collectively in the broader interest of the country. On chieftaincy disputes, he expressed concern about disagreements over succession, customary authority and traditional boundaries, which he said could destroy relationships, delay development and threaten peace in communities. He advocated stronger preventive measures and peaceful resolution of such disputes through dialogue, mediation and appropriate Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms, in accordance with the law and customary practices. He said traditional leaders had a special responsibility in resolving such disagreements because of their knowledge of customary practices, family histories and community relationships. The Yagbonwura urged traditional authorities to promote a culture of dialogue rather than confrontation and place peace above personal interests. He also called for the proper documentation of customary lines of succession in traditional areas to prevent uncertainty and disputes whenever traditional vacancies occurred. He noted that although succession histories and procedures were often preserved through oral traditions and family knowledge, the absence of proper records could create challenges for future generations. He therefore urged royal families, kingmakers, Traditional Councils, elders and other customary stakeholders to collaborate in documenting recognised succession histories, customary procedures and established precedents. Such documentation, he said, would help preserve cultural heritage, guide future generations and minimise avoidable chieftaincy disputes. The Yagbonwura appealed to the Government, through the Minister responsible for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, to provide financial support for the documentation exercise.

items.title: SEC assures low-cost investment schemes to deepen financial inclusion
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has reaffirmed its commitment to deepening inclusive access to Ghana’s capital market through low-cost investment schemes, micro-investment products, crowdfunding and digital platforms, particularly for first-time and small-scale investors. Dr James Klutse Avedzi, Director-General of the SEC, assured this at the inauguration of a Technical Committee for the country’s second National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy (NFIDS) in Accra on Thursday. He said the Commission fully supported efforts to build a more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable financial ecosystem that leaves no one behind. Dr Avedzi said although Ghana had achieved 80 per cent financial access, largely through digital wallets, only 22 per cent of the population was financially healthy. He noted that many women, rural dwellers, informal sector workers, and smallholder farmers were still excluded from the formal financial system. Dr Avedzi said the SEC would ensure that the capital market played a central role in expanding investment opportunities for ordinary Ghanaians, while facilitating access to capital for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and microfinance institutions. “We’ll do that by collaborating across the financial sector, working hand in hand with the Bank of Ghana, the National Insurance Commission, the National Pensions Regulatory Authority and all stakeholders,” he said. The Commission, he said, would also promote investment in sustainable financial products to drive inclusive economic growth, making capital market operations a development priority and a shared national responsibility. Beyond expanding access, Dr Avedzi said the SEC would intensify investor education and financial literacy campaigns to equip Ghanaians with the knowledge and confidence to make informed financial decisions. He also pledged to strengthen investor protection through robust regulatory and enforcement frameworks to safeguard all investors’ savings and investments, particularly vulnerable groups. Meanwhile, members of the Diplomatic Corps pledged support for developing and implementing Ghana’s second financial inclusion strategy (2027–2031). The strategy seeks to expand access to savings, credit, insurance and secure payment services, while creating jobs, promoting entrepreneurship and driving economic growth. Ms Janine Walz, Deputy Swiss Ambassador to Ghana and Head of Cooperation, reaffirmed Switzerland’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s efforts to develop a well-functioning and inclusive financial sector as a foundation for sustainable development. The previous strategy, which covered 2018 to 2023, recorded significant gains in expanding access to credit, savings, payment and insurance services for underserved groups, supported by reforms such as mobile money interoperability and the introduction of the Ghana Card. The second strategy is expected to build on those gains, with the Government placing financial health at its centre to ensure that access to financial services translates into improved livelihoods, greater economic security and wealth creation.

items.title: L’AMMA célèbre le Maroc en musique à Casablanca
items.description: L’Association Marocaine de la Musique Andalouse (AMMA) organise, samedi 14 novembre 2026 à 20h00 au Théâtre L’Hermitage à Casablanca, une grande soirée artistique placée sous le signe de la mémoire, du patrimoine et de la célébration nationale. Intitulée « De la mémoire à la célébration, aux rythmes et aux couleurs de la nation », cette soirée entend faire dialoguer histoire et musique à travers un programme consacré aux grandes expressions du patrimoine musical marocain. Organisé sous l’égide du Ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et des Sports, avec le soutien de la Loterie Nationale et des Eaux Minérales d’Oulmès, l’événement mettra à l’honneur plusieurs répertoires qui constituent la richesse du patrimoine immatériel du Royaume. Sur scène, le public retrouvera l’orchestre de feu Mohamed Laarbi El Mrabet, placé sous la direction du maître Mohamed Laaroussi, aux côtés de la chanteuse et artiste Majda El Yahyaoui. La programmation proposera un voyage musical à travers différents univers : musique andalouse, Melhoun, répertoire Issawa, Gnawa et chant soufi. Une manière de mettre en lumière la diversité des traditions musicales marocaines et leur capacité à dialoguer au sein d’une même célébration. À travers cette soirée, l’AMMA souhaite également contribuer à la transmission de ce patrimoine aux nouvelles générations. L’association entend ainsi faire de la musique un vecteur de mémoire, mais aussi un moyen de renforcer le lien entre les jeunes et les différentes composantes de l’identité culturelle marocaine. Le choix de réunir plusieurs répertoires autour d’un même événement s’inscrit dans une volonté de rappeler que le patrimoine musical marocain constitue un héritage vivant. Il ne s’agit pas uniquement de préserver des traditions, mais aussi de leur donner une place dans le présent et de favoriser leur transmission. Fatima Mabchour, présidente fondatrice de l’AMMA, souligne cette dimension mémorielle et collective : « Cette manifestation rend avant tout hommage à celles et ceux qui ont écrit les plus belles pages de notre histoire. À travers la musique, nous célébrons un Maroc qui a su avancer avec courage et unité, tout en portant un regard confiant vers l’avenir » . The post L’AMMA célèbre le Maroc en musique à Casablanca appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Chiefs commend ADAMUS CEO for support to Esiama SHS
items.description: Traditional rulers and stakeholders in Esiama have commended Angela Dialla Attieh, CEO of ADAMUS Resources Limited, a subsidiary of Nguvu Mining Company Limited, for the company’s support towards the development of the Esiama Senior High Technical School (ESHTS). The commendation followed the donation of 200 tables and chairs, 150 pairs of sports shoes, and 350 sanitary pads to the school. The delegation, led by Nana Ainoo Kwagyan III, Divisional Chief of Esiama, paid its respects during a familiarisation visit to the school’s management and students, barely a week after the climax of the annual Kundum Festival. The festival, which marked the end of one harvest season and the beginning of another, highlighted the need for stakeholders to champion development initiatives within the community. The delegation included Dr George Sipa Yankey, Development Chief (Nkosuohene) of Esiama and Board Chairman of the Tema Shipyard and Dry Dock Company; Mr Joe Wise, a businessman; Nana Agyane Aka VI, Chief of Salma; and Nana Ezane Nda, Tufuhene of Esiama. Addressing the gathering, Dr Sipa Yankey, a former Minister of Health and former Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana National Gas Company Limited, said he had observed ADAMUS Resources’ significant contributions to the school’s development. He said it was important to acknowledge Madam Attieh’s efforts to encourage the company to invest further in initiatives that enhance teaching and learning. Dr Sipa Yankey noted that the donation of tables and chairs helped reduce the school’s furniture deficit, where many students previously lacked adequate desks during instructional hours. He also commended Madam Attieh for the ongoing renovation of the girls’ dormitory and plans to construct a new dormitory block for female students. He further noted that ADAMUS Resources had constructed a 15-seater ultra-modern water closet toilet facility for the school. Despite the interventions, Dr Sipa Yankey expressed concern about the poor state of the school’s science laboratory, which he said lacked the apparatus and equipment needed for practical lessons. He also raised concerns about leaking classroom roofs during the rainy season and congestion in some classrooms, challenges that continued to affect effective teaching and learning. Dr Sipa Yankey recalled that some of the classroom blocks currently in use were old and dilapidated, having served as classrooms for the former Middle School during his basic education before the institution was upgraded into a Senior High Technical School. He assured the school community of his commitment to mobilise support and advocate for additional development projects for the institution. For his part, Nana Ainoo Kwagyan III said the visit aimed to translate the commitments and aspirations expressed during the grand durbar, which marked the climax of the Kundum Festival, into tangible development outcomes. He said the increasing student population required additional infrastructure, including classroom blocks, dormitories, and teachers’ accommodation. Nana Ainoo Kwagyan assured students and staff of his determination to support efforts to secure more projects to improve teaching and learning in the school. Mr Francis Amissah, the school’s Headmaster, who led the delegation on a campus tour to inspect facilities, commended the chiefs and elders for their continued support. He highlighted several development milestones achieved through Dr Sipa Yankey’s efforts, particularly the ongoing boys’ dormitory project, which he lobbied for through Ghana Gas and which the company is currently continuing.
