items.title: Trump says he is highly unlikely to order Iran strikes if talks progress
items.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress, even as both countries reported that ​shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. “It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump told CNN in a phone interview. “The answer is, highly unlikely ‌it’s going to be necessary.” CNN did not specify exactly what it had asked Trump, who also said that if strikes resume, the US has identified potential infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges “that we can knock down in literally one hour.” Later on Sunday afternoon, Trump posted on Truth Social that “Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect” on Iran. The campaign, first reported by Reuters on Saturday, will crack down on Tehran’s movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the Caspian Sea. Trump acknowledged after the last week’s US midterm elections that ​the Iran war was a part of the reason for Republicans’ defeat, while Vice President JD Vance, seen as a potential successor to Trump when his term ends in two years, went a step further, saying definitively ​in a social media post, “The reason we lost is the war.” Trump told reporters on Sunday that “a lot of people did not like Vance’s comments on Iran.” Secretary of State Marco ⁠Rubio, widely considered another contender to succeed Trump, declined to comment on Sunday on a link between the war and the elections. “All I can tell you is that the president of the United States identified a very real threat to ​this country that existed for a very long period of time, and he addressed it,” Rubio told reporters. Asked separately about diplomatic efforts to end the war, Rubio said he did not believe a breakthrough was imminent. “The president would always prefer to solve ​this and every problem diplomatically. Sometimes that’s not possible, unfortunately. But if there’s a chance to do it. We’ll explore it. Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic,” Rubio said. Trump had been hinting that he would renew major attacks on Iran once the elections were over , but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking US and Israeli targets. Iranian media suggested that explosions in southern ​Iran on Saturday were related to Iranian military activities rather than US strikes. Iran’s state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iranian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait. Both the ​US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy. Iran’s state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iranian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said ‌two vessels had ⁠hit mines and a third had caught fire. The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait. Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on November 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets. COMMERCIAL VESSEL, OIL TANKERS HIT Since the US and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, Tehran has sought the upper hand by hitting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz to block Gulf energy exports, while US forces began blockading movements to and from Iranian ports in April. The US military said on Saturday ​evening that its air force had fired at the stern ​of a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, ⁠disabling it as it tried to get through the blockade. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through an “unauthorized route” in the Strait of Hormuz. A third tanker had also suffered an explosion and caught fire, the semi-official Fars news agency reported later. Reuters was not able to confirm any of the ​reported strikes. Monitors from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a bulk carrier and military forces were involved in an incident in the Gulf of Oman, approximately 18 nautical ​miles east of the United ⁠Arab Emirates’ city of Khor Fakkan, with damage unknown. It was unclear if it was related to the reported US attack. A conflict between Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia has escalated this month, enlarging the wider Middle East war. On Sunday, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said an administrative building belonging to state oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh had been damaged by falling debris after an attempted attack, with no injuries or fatalities reported. Qatar, which has been mediating in talks to try to end a conflict that has ⁠shaken the world ​economy, on Saturday denied reports that the US and Iran had failed to reach a deal. The Qatari prime minister had affirmed that both sides ​were continuing to work toward an agreement , it said. Iran has submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday , saying the US was reviewing it but discussions would depend on Washington first meeting Tehran’s seven demands. These include sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and war reparations, while ​Washington says nuclear issues must feature in initial talks.

items.title: Minister supports creation of up to 12 provinces
items.description: • Khawaja Asif says new units should be created on administrative grounds, not linguistic, ethnic or political lines • Calls for transfer of powers, resources from provincial capitals to local institutions • MQM-P renews demand for new administrative units; calls for ending ‘deprivation’ of urban Sindh SIALKOT / KARACHI: As a debate around the possible creation of new administrative units rages in the country, another federal minister on Sunday voiced his support for the proposal, but warned against carving out units on linguistic, ethnic or political lines. Outspoken Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who has previously voiced his support for the suggestion — first put forward by his cabinet colleague Mohsin Naqvi — said that the existing concentration of authority in provincial capitals was preventing government services and resources from reaching people at the local level. Speaking to Geo News , Mr Asif said the idea of creating new provinces had been debated for the past two months, stressing that the country could have as many as 12 if the exercise was driven by administrative needs rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations. He argued that Pakistan’s growing population called for smaller administrative units capable of delivering public services more effectively, adding that decision-making should not be confined to provincial capitals such as Lahore, Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar. Stressing the need to bring administrative authority closer to the people, Mr Asif also questioned the existing arrangement for distributing financial resources, insisting that funds provided by the federal government remained largely under the control of provincial administrations, instead of reaching local government institutions. He maintained that local bodies, which were supposed to benefit from these resources, continued to depend on provincial governments for funds and authority. The minister also urged political leaders to change their attitude towards the exercise of power, saying that as politicians, there was a temptation to exercise all the power themselves. Public representatives must remember that their authority was entrusted to them by the people, he said. Referring to past administrative arrangements, Mr Asif recalled the One Unit scheme, under which the provinces of West Pakistan were merged into a single administrative unit before the arrangement was eventually abolished. He also pointed to Afghanistan, saying the number of its provinces had increased from around eight or 10 to more than 30. The defence minister’s remarks come amid reports of a plan to divide Pakistan into 12 provinces through a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment, with a nationwide referendum also being contemplated. Media reports suggested that the proposed restructuring could involve dividing Punjab into four provinces, KP and Balochistan into three each, and Sindh into two. MQM-P renews demand Meanwhile, the Muttahida Qaumi Mov­e­ment-Pakistan (MQM-P) on Sunday vowed to mobilise its entire organisational network and parliamentary leadership for the upcoming local government elections eyeing a “historic win”, while renewing its demand for the creation of new administrative units in Sindh to ensure the devolution of powers and resources to the grassroots level. The resolve was expressed at a high-level meeting of the party’s political and administrative leadership, chaired by MQM-P Convener and Federal Minister Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui at its Bahadurabad headquarters. According to a press release, the meeting discussed a strategy to address the long-standing grievances of urban Sindh, accelerate Karachi’s development and prepare for upcoming political and local government contests. The party leadership stressed that the establishment of new administrative units was essential to empower people at the grassroots level and ensure the equitable provision of basic municipal services. It maintained that the devolution of authority and resources to lower tiers of government was necessary to address the administrative and civic challenges facing urban centres. Dr Siddiqui directed parliamentarians and organisational departments to become actively involved at the neighbourhood level and mobilise workers and residents across the city ahead of the local government elections. Speaking at the meeting, Dr Siddiqui said ending the deprivation of urban Sindh, establishing new administrative units and winning the local government elections were among the party’s foremost priorities. “The reconstruction and development of Karachi and other major urban centres of Sindh, transparent utilisation of public funds and the protection of citizens’ fundamental rights remained at the heart of the party’s political agenda,” a statement issued after the meeting quoted him as saying. He added that no political or administrative obstacle would be allowed to stand in the way of public welfare and development. The meeting also underscored the party’s determination to “restore the rightful representation of urban communities in local governance through electoral success and a stronger grassroots organisational presence”. Imran Ayub in Karachi also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Oil falls as Trump says new Iran attacks ‘unlikely’
items.description: Oil prices fell at Monday’s open after US President Donald Trump said he was highly unlikely to order new Iran ​attacks while talks to end the conflict make progress, despite both nations’ reports of attacks on ships in or near ‌the Strait of Hormuz. Brent was down 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 a barrel by 0138 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate fell 32 cents, or 0.35%, to $90.51 a barrel. The fall reversed minor gains made on Friday’s settlement as the market assessed the possibility of further US strikes on Iran, although Brent fell 17% last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start of the COVID pandemic and the biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988. “It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” ​Trump told CNN in a phone interview . “The answer is, highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary.” Trump had hinted at renewing attacks on Iran after last week’s US midterm elections , but there has been no sign ​of a large-scale US military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking ​US and Israeli targets. Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, called Trump’s comments “more measured” but said “the market ‌is ⁠still waiting to see whether the midterms have produced a lasting shift in Trump’s approach to the conflict, or whether this is just another temporary change in tone.” Oil is headed for a glut again as recovering Middle Eastern oil flows, rising production from other countries ​, and weak demand have pushed global supply above consumption, JPMorgan said in a report on Friday, estimating a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October. On Sunday, Iraq reached an understanding with the US ​to allow ⁠Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in an interview with Al Jazeera. He said Iraq’s losses from the Iran ⁠war ​and disruptions to oil exports had reached $60 billion. Separately, the ​Houthis claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Aramco’s offices in the capital, Riyadh, on Sunday that left windows blown ​out but no reported casualties.

items.title: Indicted judge who sits in judgement can only deliver injustice, by Owei Lakemfa
items.description: Ten weeks before the contentious and increasingly violent general elections in the country, Justice Peter Odo Lifu of the Federal High Court Abuja nullified the leadership of one of the two main opposition parties, the African Democratic Congress, ADC. He did not only purport to remove the David Mark-Rauf Aregbesola leadership of the party, but also nullified the nomination of all the party’s candidates in the elections. This includes that of its Presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. The Lifu judgement was made a day after the party launched its presidential campaigns in Sokoto. On the day of the judgement, the ADC Presidential train had moved to Kebbi State where it was attacked by thugs. This attack was not surprising. In fact, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC Presidential train of Peter Obi holds the record of suffering the most attacks in the country. In broad day light with cameras rolling, it has been attacked by thugs in Edo, Benue, Cross Rivers, and most recently, Delta State. The most recent attack on the African Action Congress, AAC Presidential team was perhaps the most graphic and documented. It was an attack in a restaurant in Ado Ekiti carried out by clearly identifiable criminals captured in various video recordings and CCTV camera. The ruling All Progressives Congress, APC has also recorded attacks. An APC campaign convoy headed for a rally in Funtua, Katsina State was attacked on the Yashi-Funtua road resulting in fourteen arrests. In the same state, two APC supporters were reportedly killed in Yankara while heading for a pro-Governor Dikko Radda rally. In Zaria, Kaduna State, APC campaign vehicles were reportedly attacked in September, 2026. Woven into this rising political violence are the continued attacks by terrorists and bandits across the country. All these are ominous signs of what 2027 might hold for the country, only for Justice Lifu, a judge indicted on Tuesday, June 16, 2026 by the Court of Appeal, to return to his judicial rascality and, attempt on Thursday, November 5, 2026 to set the political system on fire. Lifu had on June 15, 2026 deregistered the ADC and four other political parties. What irked the Appeal Court was that twenty four days earlier, it had ordered a stay of proceedings in the suit and, this had been brought to the attention of Lifu in open court. But the High Court judge willfully decided to override the decision of the higher court and, in fact, sat on appeal over it. It seemed nothing mattered to Lifu including the facts of the case before him. Clearly, whatever gains he hoped to get, outweighed the consequences he thought he could suffer by his judicial recklessness. A clearly angry Court of Appeal, reversed Lifu’s judgment describing it as a: “brazen violation of the hierarchy of the court and the 1999 Constitution”. It declared Lifu as being unfit to be a judge and that his actions are: “the highest form of judicial impertinence (and) judicial rascality” Many weighed in to protect the integrity of the judiciary and save the country from avoidable anarchy. In my June 22, 2026 column titled ‘Anarchism in judicial robes’ I submitted that: “Justice Lifu should take a bow from the bench and save the institution further embarrassment. But if he does not, the judiciary should show him the exit.” But over four months later, neither has happened and Lifu continues to roll on; a loose canon in the judicial system. This slow nature of justice or the judiciary, is what has enabled Lifu to return and practically pass the same judgement over which the Court of Appeal has sat; the purported removal of the Mark-Aregbesola leadership, the nullification of the party’s candidates and, other party decisions submitted to the Independent Electoral Commission, INEC. Lifu in his latest judgement, sat on appeal in the July 2, 2026 judgement of Justice Musa S. Liman equally of the Federal High Court, Abuja. In his Judgement in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025 instituted by Hon. Leke Abejide, Justice Liman affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-Aregbesola leadership. He specifically ruled that the July 2, 2025 handover of the ADC to the Mark-Aregbesola leadership and, the follow up July 29, 2025 NEC meeting which formally handed over the party leadership, was legal and, in compliance with the ADC constitution and the Electoral Act. Justice Liman further ruled that the matter of party leadership is an internal affair of the party and, that the High Court lacked jurisdiction to hear the case. He directed INEC to recognize the Mark-Aregbesola leadership. The INEC complied with the judgement. So, when four months later, Lifu assumed jurisdiction to hear the leadership case and, ruled that the handover was, contrary to Justice Liman’s judgement, unconstitutional, he was actually sitting on appeal over the judgment of a court of concurrent jurisdiction. The judiciary may not be blamed for producing Lifu as a judge or failing to rein him in after the Court of Appeal had indicted him and, ruled him unfit to sit on the bench. It might simply be a case of having many Lifus in its ranks. Just on November 3, 2026, the National Judicial Council, NJC under the chairmanship of the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun took disciplinary actions against nine judicial officers for various infractions. It suspended three judges for one year each without pay, with two of them barred from elevation for three years . It also issued letters of warning and caution to the other six for alleged breaches of judicial conduct. Suspended is Justice Hannatu Mohammed Kabir of the Nasarawa State High Court for the unlawful detention of a litigant for 58 days without proper contempt proceedings over alleged disobedience of court orders. Grand Kadi Mohammed Sani Salihu of the Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal was punished over his involvement in reopening a judgment delivered by the FCT Upper Area Court, constituting a committee to review the judgment and, subsequently assigning the matter to a Higher Sharia Court judge, who received fresh evidence and delivered another judgment. This, the NJC held: “amounted to an appeal against a valid judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction…” This is the same act of Justice Lifu. The third judge, Justice Sobere Biambo of the Rivers State High Court was sanctioned for the issuance of bench warrants and imposition of N300,000 fines on each of the litigants in a civil dispute without due process. I have no doubt that an indicted judge like Lifu who continues to sit in judgement, cannot deliver justice. The NJC needs to move swiftly on matters such as Lifu’s which are capable of plunging the country into chaos, worsen insecurity and, derailing the political system. The post Indicted judge who sits in judgement can only deliver injustice, by Owei Lakemfa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Trump says after midterms defeat his immigration crackdown was ‘too tough’
items.description: US President Donald Trump has said his immigration crackdown was “too tough”, marking one of his clearest public retreats from a defining plank of his political agenda, following his party’s drubbing in the midterm elections. In an interview with CBS’ 60 Minutes programme, Trump said he believed he deserved an “A plus” for drastically limiting illegal border crossings, but he had been politically “hurt” by sweeping deportations. He acknowledged this despite his homeland security department insisting it wasn’t backing away from the crackdown. Election-day polling showed immigration was the third most important issue for midterm voters, after the economy and the state of democracy. In historically conservative states like Texas, a swing of Latino voters towards Democrats helped seal the Democratic Party’s landslide majorities in Congress. The president told 60 Minutes that immigration “both helped and hurt” his fellow Republicans in Tuesday’s midterms. “I think I got an A plus for closing up the border,” he said in the programme that aired on Sunday evening. He added: “For getting people out, I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out. “But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally.” “I think it was too tough,” the president said. Trump also said he’d “love to do something on immigration” with congressional Democrats, without offering details. In a previous interview with 60 Minutes a year ago, a defiant Trump insisted his administraiton’s immigration raids “haven’t gone far enough”. His conciliatory words on Sunday were an abrupt change in tone from a White House statement earlier in the day to the BBC. A spokeswoman vowed “the administration will not slow down its efforts to arrest and deport criminal illegal aliens who terrorise our communities”. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) also showed no sign of a U-turn on Sunday. “ICE is NOT backing away or slowing down,” a DHS spokesperson told the BBC. Following Tuesday’s electoral losses, Vice-President JD Vance had appeared receptive to adjusting their immigration strategy. “I’m open to the idea that we should change enforcement – by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labour, for instance,” Vance wrote in a lengthy online post reflecting on the results. However, Trump’s promotion on Friday of immigration hawk Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff signalled no climbdown from the administration. Stephen Miller has been a close adviser to Trump for years Miller is widely seen as the architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policy during the first and second Trump presidencies. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) sources told CBS that in recent weeks officials have been instructed to aim for about 2,700 arrests of illegal immigrants per day, an increase from an earlier 2,000 daily arrest target. Enforcement sweeps this year spurred anti-ICE demonstrations in cities including Chicago, Minneapolis and Los Angeles. In Minneapolis, two US protesters, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, were fatally shot by immigration agents.

items.title: Will the election hold? By Suleiman A. Suleiman
items.description: Will the 2027 general elections hold as currently scheduled? There are compelling legal, logistical, and contingency reasons to doubt that the elections will hold as presently scheduled for January 16 and February 6, 2027, for the federal and state elections, respectively. First, the entire election is already in a legal peril. According to an INEC press release dated 26th October, 2026, the Commission claims to have conducted a physical display of what it calls “preliminary” Register of Voters at registration areas nationwide from 9th to 15th October, and published this “preliminary” copy online on 26th October. INEC then added that: “Meanwhile, the commission continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the final register of voters on 15th December 2026”. There are a thousand and one legal problems with this release because nearly everything INEC says in this release is not only a direct violation of the Electoral Act 2026, but puts the entire election into a legal peril. By publishing the preliminary voter’s register on 26th October, and promising to release the certified copy of the register on 15th December, INEC has already breached the law, twice. The wording of Section 9(6) of the Electoral Act 2026 could not be clearer, as it says: “The registration of voters, updating and revision of the Register of Voters under this section shall stop not later than 90 days before any election covered by this Act”. Moreover, Section 19(1) of the Act further provides that: “Subject to the provisions of section 9 (6) of this Act, the Commission shall, not later than 90 days to a general election, appoint a period of seven days during which a copy of the voters’ register for each Local Government, Area Council or Ward shall be displayed or published for public scrutiny at every registration area and on its official website or any website established by the Commission for that purpose”. One does not need to be a lawyer to grasp the legal force of these provisions. First, these are legal provisions, not mere administrative timelines that INEC or anyone can bend or ignore at will. The provisions require INEC to ensure that continuous voter registration, publication, claims and objections, and revisions and clean-up of the Voter Register “shall stop not later than 90 days before any election covered by this Act”. That deadline is 18 October, 2026 and cannot be extended or changed unless the law is amended. In other words, the Electoral Act requires INEC to have a final copy of the register of Voters latest by 18th October, 2026 for the opening presidential and national assembly elections on January 16, 2027. INEC does not have the final Voter register, and in its own words, it would not have it until 32 days before the election on 15th December, 2026. That is in clear violation of the Electoral Act. But it gets worse. The word “shall” is one of the strongest forms of language use in any body of laws, and almost always used as a categorical command. In this case, the command is clear: there can be no further work on the Voter Register after 18th October, 2026, which has already elapsed. This means that the processing of “claims and objections” arising from the publication of the preliminary register, and “preparatory to the certification and publication of the final register of voters on 15th December 2026”, to quote INEC directly once again, are all null and void under the law. If INEC’s yet to be released final Voter Register is already an illegality, then the election is also legally voided long before any votes are cast. This is not merely the opinion of a newspaper columnist. It is a matter that lawyers are discussing publicly, including Festus Okoye, himself an election litigation expert and former INEC Commissioner for Public Information and Education. For INEC, the legal banana peel it finds itself sleep-walking over is trouble enough, but more troubling still is the legal uncertainty surrounding the candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), one of the principal opposition parties in the elections. INEC published its candidate lists on October 31. However, on November 5, the Federal High Court delivered a judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC and invalidating the party’s primary election processes conducted under that leadership. This changed everything. The ruling APC may be happy that ADC’s presidential and other down-ballot candidates are presently in a legal limbo about their candidacy arising from this latest court judgment. However, INEC too is in a legal limbo, and indeed the entire election and the country. Section 32(1) of the Electoral Act 2026 provides that: “The Commission shall, at least 60 days before the day of the election, publish by displaying or causing to be displayed at the relevant office or offices of the Commission and on the Commission’s website, a statement of the full names and addresses of all candidates standing nominated”. The deadlines for this are 17th November for the federal elections, and 8th December for state elections. Because the ADC has appealed the ruling, INEC must wait until the case is finally decided in the courts. If INEC updates and publishes its final list of candidates without hundreds of candidates of a major opposition party, then it would not only be acting prejudicially in relation to the courts, but also destroying the credibility of the elections completely even before any votes are cast. If INEC does not publish the list by 17th November—in eight days—then any subsequent list published after this date would be in breach of the law, and therefore, null and void. This means that there is real risk of the entire slate of candidates across ALL THE PARTIES being voided, not just the ADC candidates. It is not the ADC alone that should be worried about this latest court case, the ruling APC and other parties have even more to worry about. In other words, with just 68 days left until the election, Nigeria has no legally binding Register of Voters and no legally binding final list of candidates for the election. These legal problems facing INEC are serious enough to scuttle the election, but they also have compounded INEC’s logistical challenges which is a nightmare even at the best of times. INEC cannot produce several critical election materials—ballot papers, electoral and collation forms, etc—without a complete and final list of candidates and voter’s register. Because of the security implications of these documents, they have normally been produced outside of Nigeria and transported into the country. In addition, they would need to be transported across all the 36 states capitals for onward distribution to INECs more than 190,000 polling units on election day. Most of these logistics are not under the direct control of INEC. And with just 68 days left until the election, these massive logistical operations are already a near impossibility to pull off. As far as INEC’s elections are concerned, we may be sleep-walking back to 2007, the most discredited elections in Nigerian history. Since at least 2011, Nigeria’s elections have been improving in both process and integrity of the elections, including the 2023 election. You would think that for a president much touted as a democrat, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu would be deeply concerned about all these serious developments threatening his own re-election. Perhaps, he is. There is little evidence, however, that the government has risen to the urgency of the situation. The question then is how we arrive here, and what can be done to save the day. The answer is pretty simple. The INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, is incapable of doing this job. The shoe is bigger than his feet, and more than that, his two immediate predecessors also tower heads and shoulders above him in competence and the capacity to do this specific job. The political and legal battels aside, the lack of capacity of the current INEC Chairman is the single most important reason for how we got here. The solution must therefore also be directed there. What INEC needs, and what the urgency of the situation deserves, is a new pair of hands to steady the ship. Otherwise, we will be risking everything. The post Will the election hold? By Suleiman A. Suleiman appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Firecrackers, earthen lamps and sweets — Hindu community shares colours of Diwali
items.description: A woman holds an ignited sparkler as people watch the fireworks during a Diwali celebration, while (right) another woman decorates a rangoli pattern with earthen lamps at Shri Swami Narayan Temple on M.A. Jinnah Road.—Shakil Adil/ White Star / PPI KARACHI: Firecrackers went off, sparks flew, and earthen lamps glowed as the Hindu community in Pakistan celebrated Diwali, the festival of lights, on Sunday. Diwali is celebrated on the new-moon night, known as Amavas during the Hindu month of Kartika. Since the sky is dark at the time, the fireworks triumph over the darkness. The festival also serves as a remembrance of other triumphs such as of good over evil, of knowledge over ignorance and hope over despair. It is a celebration of the victorious return of Shri Rama Chandra to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile. According to Hindu scriptures, Rama and his wife Sita, along with younger brother Lakshmana, took refuge in the forest after their kingdom was taken from them. Later, Ravana, a demon king from Sri Lanka, abducted Sita and took her to his kingdom. Rama and Lakshmana, with the help of Hanuman, raise an army that builds a bridge from Tamil Nadu to Sri Lanka to reach Ravana’s kingdom and rescue Sita. They return triumphant after killing Ravana and are welcomed home by their people who lit clay lamps along their path. While commemorating the happy occasion, the Hindu community also decorates their home entrances, especially the floor there with pretty colourful designs known as rangoli. This ritual is associated with Goddess Lakshmi, the deity of wealth and prosperity, who is believed to visit clean and brightly lit homes on the day. Muslims also join festivities to promote interfaith harmony, pluralism So even though the main focus remains on lighting up the skies and one’s surroundings, there are also many preparations underway in the days leading up to Diwali. These include house cleaning and decorating, preparing sweetmeats, putting together new outfits and buying jewellery and gifts. These preparations are also important but should not tire you so much that you are unable to enjoy the festival itself. Therefore, it is always better to prepare in advance. This year, there were many Diwali markets all over Karachi to help people prepare for the festival in advance. There was the biggest-ever Diwali Bazar at the Faizy Rameen Auditorium along with the one at the ground behind the Shri Swami Narayan Temple, at the Shri Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple in Clifton and also at the Port Grand where entrance was free for the Hindu community. A woman holds an ignited sparkler as people watch the fireworks during a Diwali celebration, while (right) another woman decorates a rangoli pattern with earthen lamps at Shri Swami Narayan Temple on M.A. Jinnah Road.—Shakil Adil/ White Star / PPI As a good show of harmony and pluralism, many Muslims also enjoyed the festival of lights with their Hindu friends by lighting diyas and sharing sweets. Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

Pope Leo urges men to respect their wives
items.description: FLORIDA: Pope Leo XIV told men to treat their wives with respect, as he concluded the first leg of his tour of Latin America, which is plagued by gender-based violence. “Dear fathers and grandfathers… treat your wives with respect, ask for forgiveness and live with integrity, even when doing so requires sacrifice,” the head of the Catholic Church said during a homily in Uruguay. Over 3,800 women were killed in Latin America and the Caribbean in 2024 because of their gender, according to the UN’s regional economic mission. Over the last five years, the region has recorded nearly 20,000 femicides, most of them committed by the victim’s current or former partner. Leo is on a 12-day tour of the continent where he served as a missionary and a bishop before becoming pope. He wrapped up the first leg of his visit in largely secular Uruguay with an open-air mass outside a basilica in the south-central city of Florida. Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Rawalpindi’s historic buildings crumble amid official apathy
items.description: Old buildings, temples and Gurdwaras in Rawalpindi tell the story of the garrison city’s majestic past, when Hindus and Sikhs made up a dominant share of its population before the partition of the Indian subcontinent. However, these buildings are now in a state of disrepair, as little has been done to preserve them over the past 79 years. Jamia Masjid in Rawalpindi stands tall but is in need of repairs. Though the history of Rawalpindi dates back to the arrival of Alexander in India, its architecturally splendid buildings provide ample opportunities for history lovers to explore the city’s past. However, many of these structures are gradually disappearing with the passage of time. The old bridge over Leh Nullah, which connected the city and cantonment areas during the British era, is gradually losing its wooden structure to theft, while a junkyard has been established on the bridge. A visit to the narrow streets of the downtown area reveals numerous havelis, temples and Gurdwaras that reflect Rawalpindi’s past. The spires of temples and domes of Gurdwaras can still be seen from the roads, but none of these buildings has been declared a national heritage site. Moreover, the land attached to temples and Gurdwaras is rapidly being lost to encroachments. A view of Rawalpindi’s downtown area where the spires of temples and mosques recall a time when Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs lived together in the city. Mandir Kalyan Das, located in Kohati Bazaar, is one of the largest temples in the garrison city. It was constructed in 1850 by a wealthy Hindu resident of Rawalpindi, Kalyan Das, belonging to the Suri family. A veranda adjoining the courtyard of Sujan Singh Haveli in Rawalpindi’s downtown area. Old temples and the majestic building of the Gurdwara of Rai Bahadur Sujan Singh, constructed during the pre-partition era, are among the historically significant structures in the city. However, they have never received much attention from the government. An old wooden balcony structure in Sarafa Bazaar, which is rapidly disappearing. In Raja Bazaar, there was an old temple opposite Narankari Bazaar. The temple was constructed in 1880 by Shrimati Devi in memory of her husband. At present, however, its main room has been sealed, while the rest of the building has been rented out to traders who have established their outlets there. The old structure of Mohan Singh Haveli in the garrison city of Rawalpindi. — Photos by Mohammad Asim Kali Mata Temple is located in Moti Bazaar. After the partition of the Indian subcontinent, the temple was closed and handed over to the Evacuee Trust Property Board (ETPB) as there were fewer Hindus living in the city. In Purana Qila, a gate was constructed in 1896. The bazaar was then known as Lakhshami Narayan Bazaar. A temple can be found at the top of the hill. Old houses with balconies, constructed more than 200 years ago, are still standing along the main road. A more than 130-year-old bridge connecting Raja Bazaar with the cantonment areas is also gradually disappearing due to the apathy of the archaeology department and local administration. The truss bridge, made of wood and iron, stands over Leh Nullah. However, scrap dealers have removed much of the precious deodar wood (Cedrus deodara) installed as girders of the bridge. Another historic structure is the 136-year-old majestic Sujan Singh Haveli, located in the narrow streets of Bhabara Bazaar. It was constructed by Sikh political figure Sardar Sujan Singh. The four-storey haveli, constructed in 1890, is a fine specimen of brick masonry. Facing the street, it features a front veranda and a central entrance, giving it a majestic appearance. Its 45 spacious rooms have English tiles and Kashmiri wood carvings. The building was once an outstanding example of Kashmiri woodwork, but the passage of time has faded its glorious past. The old Presidency, formerly the State Guest House on The Mall, which has now been converted into Fatima Jinnah Women University (FJWU), also needs the attention of the relevant departments for its preservation. Built to accommodate the Prince of Wales during his visit to India under the reign of Queen Victoria, the grand building on The Mall has served as the Presidency, a state guest house and is now the campus of Fatima Jinnah Women University. Construction of the building began in 1898, as Prince Edward (later King Edward VII) was scheduled to visit India. However, his visit was postponed following the death of Queen Victoria, after which he became king. A senior official of the Evacuee Trust Property Board told Dawn that more than 1,000 buildings in the district were under the administrative control of the ETPB. However, due to limited funds, the board could not make efforts to protect them from the vagaries of weather. He said the ETPB had only managed to protect the properties from encroachments and maintain their records. However, he added that the status of properties already given on rent would not be changed. When contacted, Punjab Archaeology Director General Zaheer Abbas Malik said the Punjab government had devised a plan to preserve the historical buildings in Rawalpindi city. “It is a complete heritage city plan, and we are covering temples and other historic structures,” he said. Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

items.title: PM raises youth loan amount, lowers minimum age limit
items.description: LAHORE: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has increased the limit of personal loans available under the Youth Business and Agriculture Loan schemes, and reduced the minimum age limit to allow 18-year-olds to avail the scheme as well. Chairing a meeting to review progress and implementation of the PM’s Youth Business and Agriculture Loan schemes on Sunday, the prime minister directed that the personal loan limit be enhanced from Rs7.5 million to Rs25m, which would be provided in easy installments. According to the PM’s Office, an amount of Rs 292 billion has been allocated this year for disbursement of loans to the youth under these schemes. Personal loan limit enhanced to Rs25m; scheme extended to include 18-year-olds PM Shehbaz appreciated the efforts of Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and his team, and considered various measures to empower the youth, provide them with business opportunities and increase their participation in the agricultural sector. The PM directed that 30pc of loans be allocated to women, so that they can become economically independent and increase their participation in business activities. He also ordered that the minimum age limit for obtaining loans be reduced from 21 years to 18 years, so that young people can be provided with opportunities to start businesses and participate in agricultural activities at an early age. PM Shehbaz also called on the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (Smeda) to provide all possible assistance to the youth under the scheme, including business start-up guidance, consultancy and technical assistance. The meeting was told that since January 2023, loans have been provided to 581,341 young people, worth around Rs 313.9 billion. It is estimated that Rs292bn will be disbursed to 266,700 recipients during the fiscal year 2026-27. The meeting was attended by Finance Minister Aurangzeb, SAPM on Youth Affairs Rana Mashhood Ahmed Khan and SAPM on Political Affairs Talha Burki. Separately, Federal Minister for Defence Production Raza Hayat Harraj called on PM Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday. According to the PM’s Office, the two men discussed matters of mutual interest and the country’s political and economic situation. Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz said he was deeply saddened by the tragic shooting incident in Krakow, which has resulted in the loss of precious human lives and left several others injured. “Pakistan stands in solidarity with the people and Government of Poland in this moment of profound grief,” he wrote on X. Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Senate opposition leader urges govt to stay out of Yemen
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Sunday urged the government to keep Pakistan out of the conflict in Yemen and instead pursue a mediatory role, warning that violating the unanimous parliamentary resolution of 2015 would damage national interests. Addressing the Shuhada-i-Muqawamat and Tajdeed-i-Ahd Conference organised by the Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM), the party chief reminded attendees that parliament had unanimously decided in 2015 that Pakistan would not become part of the Yemen conflict or send its troops there. “On whose authority is Pakistan being made a party to this conflict?” he asked, calling on the government to pull the country out of what he described as a dangerous situation. Condemning attacks on Yemen, the opposition leader said the Yemeni people were being punished for supporting Pale­s­tinians and raising their voice against Israeli aggression. Ignoring the will of parliament on the matter, he said, would undermine the country’s national interests, sovereignty and public aspirations. MWM chief says abandoning 2015 parliamentary resolution may harm national interests; uarges govt to opt for mediation instead “Yemen has offered Pakistan a mediatory role. I have written to the prime minister, drawing his attention to the sensitivity of the matter,” he said, claiming that he also had asked the foreign minister about how the country could become a party to the conflict while playing the role of a mediator. He urged the government to focus on a ceasefire, negotiations and regional peace instead of involving the country in a war against another Muslim state, noting that Yemen had expressed solidarity with Gaza and challenged Israeli interests. The opposition leader also condemned US and Israeli aggression against Iran, saying the attacks and assassination of Iran’s supreme leader were apparently aimed at intimidating the Iranian nation and forcing it to surrender within hours. However, he said, the strategy failed as Iran demonstrated courage, wisdom and resilience. The opposition leader said plans by the US and Israel to redraw the regional map, divide countries and eliminate resistance movements posed a serious threat to regional peace. He maintained the conflict was linked to the future of the entire region, the Palestinian issue and the collective interests of the Muslim world. He described the government’s excessive praise of US President Donald Trump and efforts to secure his goodwill, including proposals for a Nobel Peace Prize nomination, as contrary to national dignity. Turning to domestic affairs, Mr Abbas said that Pakistan belongs to its people and was not the property of any individual, elite group or political mafia. The state must protect the fundamental rights of all citizens, including people in Balochistan, Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir, he said. Expressing concern over political freedoms, he argued the use of state force could not resolve public grievances. He called for an opportunity for former prime minister Imran Khan to play a role in promoting national reconciliation, describing him as a major political asset who enjoyed the confidence of a substantial section of the population. The conference was also addressed by MWM Vice Chairman Allama Syed Ahmed Iqbal Rizvi, Chief Organiser Syed Nasir Abbas and Central Secretary for Political Affairs Syed Asad Abbas Naqvi. The speakers paid tribute to those killed in resistance movements, reaffir­med solidarity with Palestine and Yemen, and called for national sovereignty, unity and supremacy of the Constitution. Published in Dawn, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Maritime Trade: Cashing on shifting trade routes, ME conflict
items.description: With sufficient capacity, agile policy responses and unusually effective public-private collaboration, Pakistan is well-positioned to capitalise on shifting trade routes amid Middle East turmoil, turning short-term gains into lasting economic advantage. Building on March 2025’s tariff cuts and cargo discounts, the government introduced transshipment incentives in August 2026 under a unified regulatory framework for all ports, announced by Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, to simplify operations. It activated slab-based concessions, with 20-80pc discounts on wet cargo vessels, wharfage rebates of 20-80pc with 14 days free terminal storage facility at the Karachi Port Trust (KPT). The Port Qasim Authority (PQA) offers 100pc waiver on wharfage and 7-21 days of free storage, while all four private container operators, Karachi International Container Terminal (KICT), South Asia Pakistan Terminal (SAPT), Karachi Gateway Terminal Ltd (KGTL) and Qasim International Container Terminal (QICT), have cut terminal handling charges by up to 25pc. Pakistan has introduced regulatory reforms to boost port competitiveness and attract international shipping lines; data indicates a record surge in number of ships at Karachi Port, attracting foreign shipping and maritime services companies Besides, Pakistan has introduced regulatory reforms to boost port competitiveness and attract international shipping lines. Customs measures now permit off-dock transshipment, facilitate bulk, break-bulk and vehicle cargo, and enable sea-to-air transfers. Faster clearance, pre-arrival declarations, expanded scanning, round-the-clock examinations and electronic delivery orders are aimed at cutting delays and procedural bottlenecks. Reflecting growing international interest, Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) launched its weekly Premium IPAK direct service linking Karachi with Europe through Karachi Gateway Terminal Limited (KGTL) in October 2026. A new weekly feeder service connecting Karachi with Khor Fakkan, UAE, further strengthens Gulf connectivity and prospects for additional transshipment business. Dredging of Karachi Port’s navigation channel, scheduled for completion by December 2026, is expected to accommodate larger vessels and reduce trade logistics costs. Meanwhile, the KPT has stepped up engagement with major international shipping lines to attract more vessel calls, direct services and transshipment cargo. These efforts, backed by competitive incentives, regulatory facilitation and coordination with private terminal operators, have helped the port achieve record transshipment volumes. Karachi Port climbed 30 places to 69th in the Container Port Performance Index 2025. Its Port Liner Shipping Connectivity Index score rose from 309 in Q1 2026 to 357 in Q3. Pakistan advanced from 35th to 34th in global Liner Shipping Connectivity Index. “We cannot afford to squander this opportunity to step out of the shadows. Our goal is not to capitalise on temporary regional disruptions but to translate this opening into sustained maritime trade and investment, positioning Pakistan as a leading reliable and competitive shipping hub,” a senior official said, requesting anonymity. Private stakeholders believe that timely reforms and port expansion can finally help Pakistan capitalise on its strategic geographical location. Partially available official data indicates a record surge in vessel calls, including mother ships, robust transshipment activity, efficient container handling, rising number of ships at anchorage and growing demand for ancillary services such as warehousing and bunkering, attracting foreign shipping and maritime services companies to Pakistan. According to the KPT, it has sustained growth trajectory following a record FY2025-26, when cargo handling reached an all-time high of 55.438m tonnes and container throughput hit 2.749m (20-foot equivalent unit) TEUs with over 2,100 vessel calls. Growth continued in July-October 2026, with cargo throughput rising 3.8pc to 19.286m tonnes from 18.581m tonnes a year earlier. Export cargo grew 10.5pc and dry bulk handling surged 26.1pc, while vessel calls increased by 13.7pc to 764 from 672 last year. Beyond its operational performance, Karachi Port contributes significantly to public revenues, with the KPT paying Rs12bn annually in federal taxes and Rs5bn to Sindh. The provincial government also collects Rs160bn annually through the Sindh Infrastructure Development Cess (SIDC) on goods entering the province through Karachi Port and Port Qasim. KPT Chairman retired Rear Admiral Shahid Ahmed laments that despite substantial SIDC collections, dilapidated roads linking Karachi’s ports to industrial zones and national highways continue to delay cargo movement and inflate logistics costs. He proposed earmarking 50pc of SIDC revenue for upgrading and maintaining port access roads through coordinated federal and provincial efforts involving relevant stakeholders. The Karachi Port recorded notable gains in global performance benchmarks, climbing 30 places to 69th in the Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) 2025. Its Port Liner Shipping Connectivity Index (PLSCI) score rose from 309 in Q1 2026 to 357 in Q3, while Pakistan advanced from 35th to 34th in global Liner Shipping Connectivity Index (LSCI), reflecting improved port efficiency, connectivity and competitiveness. Mr Ahmed says the KPT is expanding capacity, connectivity and maritime services through dredging, modernisation and investment. Bunkering services launched with Vitol in November 2025 have served over 170 vessels. Projects offered to investors include 250 acres for terminal development, 140 acres for a Marine Business District and Manora Shipyard. “The KPT will prioritise direct shipping services, transshipment, faster cargo clearance, terminal expansion and improved road-rail connectivity, alongside digitalisation through enterprise resource planning, vessel traffic management and integration with the Port Community System,” the KPT chairman says. Muhammad Rajpar, former chairman of the Pakistan Ship’s Agents Association, welcomes the progress, citing reduced port and terminal transshipment tariffs, risk-based customs scanning and non-intrusive inspections. Other measures include direct engagement with global shipping lines, permission to use off-dock terminals for transshipment, introduction of feeder services and removal of Pakistani ports from Lloyd’s war-risk list. Relocating long-stay auction containers to off-dock facilities has also freed valuable port space for transshipment cargo, he adds. M H Lodhi, managing director of Monsoon Winds Maritime Services, says international collaboration in port modernisation, shipbuilding, green shipping, logistics and technology and skills development can leverage Pakistan’s strategic location to enhance its global trade competitiveness and sustain maritime growth. Published in Dawn, The Business and Finance Weekly, November 9th, 2026

items.title: High cost of crumbling infrastructure in Karachi
items.description: For thousands of Karachi’s industrial workers, the daily commute is less about distance and more about endurance. Muhammad Ali leaves his Baloch Colony home an hour before his 8am shift at a SITE area pharmaceutical plant. While he can zip 14 kilometres to Nazimabad in 15 minutes via the Karsaz corridor, the final 6km crawl to his factory takes twice as long, choked by potholes and gridlock. Across town in the Korangi Industrial Area, refinery worker Ishtiaq Ali loses four hours a day to public transport navigating endless construction and broken roads. In Pakistan’s largest industrial city, crumbling infrastructure and traffic bottlenecks have turned the simple act of going to work into an exhausting daily ordeal. The strain is not felt by workers alone. Every day, fleets of heavy vehicles transporting raw materials and finished goods through Karachi’s industrial zones – from SITE and Korangi to Landhi, North Karachi, and Federal B Area – are trapped in hours of gridlock. For the thousands of enterprises powering the nation’s economy, these dilapidated roads are more than a nuisance; they are a direct hit to the bottom line, bleeding capital through inflated fuel bills, damaged cargo, and costly delays. Dilapidated roads are inflicting huge financial losses on industrialists through rising fuel costs, longer travel time But commuting is only one of the problems confronting the city’s industrial zones. Poor sanitation, water shortages, ineffective waste-disposal systems and deteriorating drainage networks have added to the difficulties faced by businesses and workers. Yet the condition of the infrastructure serving these industrial hubs raises questions about whether essential public services are keeping pace with their economic importance. Earlier last month, the situation compelled Karachi’s industrial, business and trade community to come together and openly voice concerns over, what they described as, the economic cost of civic mismanagement that is driving up production costs and undermining competitiveness. At a meeting, representatives of Karachi-based trade bodies and industrial town associations questioned how the country’s commercial capital that contributes around 67pc of federal revenue and 54pc of national exports “continues to suffer from crumbling roads, acute water shortages, unreliable utilities, deteriorating sewerage and rampant street crime”. The condition of the infrastructure serving the industrial hubs raises questions about whether essential public services are keeping pace with their economic importance. While calling for an urgent, coordinated drive to “rescue Karachi from its deepening civic and economic crisis”, Zubair Motiwala, the chairman of Businessmen Group, has made it clear that their criticism was not aimed at creating any political or administrative controversy, but it was for a liveable, secure and economically competitive Karachi. However, an industrialist, who attended the meeting but doesn’t want to be named, says that the participants openly expressed their frustration with the PPP administration in the province and lamented that despite ruling Sindh for the past 18 years, the party has ignored the infrastructure that is still in a shambles. “The seriousness of the provincial government can be gauged from the fact that it had, in December 2025, approved over Rs9 billion for urgent road repairs and infrastructure maintenance in Karachi’s industrial areas, but even after 10 months, the work remains incomplete or has not even begun.” The industrialist was referring to the allocation for the uplift of industrial areas by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah.Recently, Korangi Industrial Trading Estate CEO Saleemuz Zaman highlighted the urgent need for sewerage and infrastructure improvements in areas adjoining the main roads of his industrial estate at the groundbreaking ceremony of the project to improve infrastructure. “The infrastructure challenges are so extensive that the Rs2bn allocation is insufficient to address all the requirements,” he told the participants in the ceremony. Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab assured the KATI members that the government would further increase the allocation in the next financial year as it knew the provision of quality roads, improved drainage systems and modern infrastructure would not only facilitate industrialists but also strengthen commercial activities, create employment opportunities and contribute to the national economy. Industrialists have identified institutional incompetence, weak accountability and administrative failures as basic reasons behind the city’s longstanding problems like road conditions, traffic diversions, water supply, drainage and waste disposal. They call for timely completion of projects, improved coordination among the relevant authorities and oversight for effective service delivery. In the words of KATI’s Deputy Patron-in-Chief Zubair Chhaya, the city’s industrialists need a coordinated and apolitical campaign to resolve worsening civic and economic issues where the priority must be implementation and accountability. Although the Sindh government is taking measures to resolve the chronic issues, until there is timely progress on the infrastructure projects, workers will continue to face lengthy commutes and industries will continue to experience cost and time overruns in transporting raw materials and finished goods. Published in Dawn, The Business and Finance Weekly, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Turning gaming talent into export earnings
items.description: Pakistan’s game development industry earns an estimated $400-480 million a year. But a large part of that money never makes it home. Faced with rules that require half of export proceeds to be converted into rupees, caps on incoming transactions, slow remittance screening and a 27pc tax on top-ups used to buy ads on platforms such as Google and Unity, many companies have registered abroad and run their finances from there. This means the industry is far bigger than the official figures suggest.Industry insiders say virtually every studio has also registered a company outside Pakistan. The reason, they explain, is that a typical game earns a profit margin of only 20-25pc, and a large part of the cost goes on marketing through international services such as Google or Unity to reach a wider audience. With so much of their spending in dollars abroad, studios say the current 50pc conversion requirement makes little business sense, and this has held back an industry (animation, graphics and games) that, according to State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB) data, accounts for 10.5pc of the $4.6 billion in IT exports recorded in FY26. Independent estimates put the figure at $500-600m and growing. According to a PSEB report, the gaming market itself is divided into mobile, console and PC games with the industry primarily dominated by mobile games with around half of the total market share. This divide is also visible in Pakistan with mobile game development being the major driver of the industry. Explaining the industry, Syed Bilal Qasim, the project director at the Centre of Excellence in Gaming & Animation (CEGA), Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, told Dawn’s Business & Finance that in Pakistan, some companies were working with internationally-established game publishers, others were self-publishing their own games, while some only focused on developing and selling game assets for in-game or platform-based stores. Other offshoots of the industry include individuals and companies providing animations and ad development services. Industry insiders highlight artificial intelligence-induced disruption coming to the industry with development cycles getting shorter, complete games developed with AI by non-developers, and restrictions and checks being imposed by platforms on AI-generated games “Game development is currently the dominant industry in Pakistan with an estimated value of more than $200m. Major focus is on mobile game development, there are also a few studios here that are working on PC gaming.” The reason for this, he elaborated, was the rapid revenue cycle of mobile game development as well as a lower investment and infrastructure requirements.In terms of the existing workforce, Pakistan had a large number of good developers but lacked skilled animators. “A small gaming studio in Lahore has at least 30 or more people working and large studios have hundreds of staffers,” he said, adding that a recent change in the industry had been brought about by Steam, a gaming platform, where many Pakistani developers were now focusing their efforts. Affak Sheikh, the co-founder of mobile gaming startup, Gamistan, said the industry had developed very rapidly in Pakistan compared to other countries in the region. “There is a mature ecosystem of mobile game development with many established companies,” he added.Bilal believed that the actual size of the industry was much bigger than the official figures as it was a norm to register a company in any country due to the restrictions imposed due to the regulatory framework in Pakistan. “For Pakistan, different numbers are quoted, starting from $200m to around $450m but the actual size is much bigger. “Other industry insiders share the same constraints and say that a company can retain half of its earnings in dollars and the rest has to be converted into rupees and this does not make business sense for this particular sector as its major cost is in dollars which has to be spent on platforms, which are outside Pakistan usually in the US. Secondly, they say, if any company brings in their entire revenue into Pakistan, then there are major roadblocks in receiving and spending money. These and high taxes become the limiting factor for the industry in Pakistan. Mr Affak said operating from Pakistan had many challenges including online platforms restricting companies based here, which he believed was due to some users abusing the system on these platforms. Explaining why companies opted to register themselves abroad, he said taxation became a major cost as there was a 27pc tax on top ups for spending money on online platforms marketing. “Studios register their companies abroad and finances are handled from abroad,” he said. Saadaan Waqar, a cofounder of Heritage Arc Studios, has been working on producing a PC and console game, which he wants to publish on Steam. This segment, he says, requires a lot more resources including the time to publish. He said: “There are not many studios working on PC and console game development in Pakistan, whereas there is a large market for this part of the industry. It has a higher cost for getting off the ground but there is a lack of developers for Unreal Engine in Pakistan, the platform on which we are developing our game. Currently, there are 10 interns, and half of them are from other countries, including the UK and USA.” He also echoed the same regulatory challenges and the workaround of getting registered abroad to avoid the higher costs of financial dealing from within Pakistan. Industry insiders who spoke to Dawn also highlighted the artificial intelligence-induced disruption coming to the industry with development cycles getting shorter, complete games developed by AI by non-developers, and restrictions and checks being imposed by platforms on AI-generated games. Bilal was of the view that AI was a major game changer for many industries, and it would certainly disrupt the gaming industry, but believed that it was too early to make a definitive prediction. However, he remained optimistic with the view that games were an art form and an artist’s creation carried a greater value. “It might become a complementary part of the whole development cycle. As for the Pakistani industry, small development teams and studios are much more agile and can quickly adapt to such disruptive changes.” Published in Dawn, The Business and Finance Weekly, November 9th, 2026

items.title: Rapatriement massif depuis la Guinée : 3 400 Burkinabè accueillis dans la ferveur à Bobo-Dioulasso par une délégation ministérielle
items.description: Dans la nuit du vendredi 6 novembre 2026, l'émotion était palpable au Stade omnisports de Bobo-Dioulasso lors de l’arrivée du tout premier convoi de Burkinabè rapatriés après leur expulsion de Guinée via le Mali. Composée de 48 autocars transportant 3 400 compatriotes pour la plupart de jeunes artisans miniers affectés par la suspension de l'orpaillage en territoire guinéen —, cette première vague a été accueillie sur place, aux environs de 21 heures, par une forte délégation gouvernementale mandatée par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Entre bilans de santé, sécurisation, soutien psychosocial et promesses de réinsertion socio-éducative, les autorités ont enclenché un dispositif d'urgence pour offrir un nouveau départ à ces rapatriés. Le vacarme des moteurs et les soupirs de soulagement ont marqué la fin d'un éprouvant périple. Ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026, sur le coup de 21 heures, les portes du Stade omnisports de Bobo-Dioulasso se sont ouvertes pour voir entrer un impressionnant convoi de 48 cars. À leur bord, 3 400 ressortissants burkinabè, contraints de quitter précipitamment la Guinée à la suite de la mesure gouvernementale guinéenne suspendant l’exploitation artisanale de l'or, regagnaient enfin la terre natale après un transit par le Mali. Preuve de l'importance accordée à ce retour par le sommet de l'État, cinq membres du gouvernement ont fait le déplacement. Dépêchée sous les instructions directes du Chef de l'État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, la délégation comprenait le ministre de l'Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l'Innovation, le Pr Adjima Thiombiano ; la ministre de la Solidarité et de la Famille, le Lieutenant-Colonel Passowindé Pélagie Kaboré/Kabré ; la ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi, Annick Pickbougoum/Zingué Ouattara ; ainsi que les ministres en charge de l'enseignement secondaire et de base, le Pr Moumouni Zoungrana et Jacques Sosthènes Dingara, aux côtés du gouverneur de la région du Guiriko, Mariama Konaté/Gnanou. Face à ces jeunes éprouvés par les aléas de l'exil minier, les représentants de l'exécutif se sont employés à réconforter les arrivants et à leur signifier la sollicitude de la Nation. « Nous rendons grâce à Dieu, ces 3 400 personnes sont rentrées à bon port » , a salué avec émotion la ministre de la Solidarité. Dès la descente des cars, le Conseil régional de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation a activé un dispositif d’accueil rigoureux et structuré en trois étapes clés : Le contrôle sécuritaire : pour s'assurer de l'identification et de la protection de tous les passagers. Le check sanitaire : afin d'examiner immédiatement l'état physique des arrivants, de dispenser les premiers soins aux blessés et de traiter les cas de maladie contractés durant le voyage ou sur les sites d'orpaillage. La prise en charge psychosociale et le profilage : un espace dédié au repos, aux premières commodités et à l'écoute des traumatismes vécus. À cette étape, les mineurs non accompagnés sont temporairement retenus pour une protection adaptée, tandis que les jeunes adultes enregistrés sont orientés pour rejoindre leurs localités et familles d'origine. Au-delà de l'urgence humanitaire immédiate, les autorités entendent transformer cette épreuve en opportunité de relèvement durable. La ministre de la Solidarité et de la Famille a détaillé les pistes d’insertion prévues par l'exécutif : le retour effectif des mineurs sur les bancs de l'école primaire et secondaire, l'apprentissage d'un métier pour ceux qui s'orienteront vers la formation professionnelle, et l'intégration directe dans les universités publiques pour les jeunes déjà titulaires du baccalauréat désireux de reprendre leurs études supérieures. À travers cette réponse globale, le pays réaffirme sa volonté de ne laisser aucun de ses enfants sur le bord du chemin. items.title: Train collision in Egypt kills 7, injures 112
items.description: The death toll from Sunday's collision between two trains in Egypt's Giza governorate has risen to seven, with 112 others injured, Egypt's Ministry of Health and Population has said. The ministry said in a statement that 45 patients had been discharged after their conditions improved and they received the necessary treatment, while seven others were expected to be discharged soon. The remaining injured were continuing to receive treatment under medical observation. Earlier in the day, the ministry said in another statement that 72 ambulances took part in rescue and evacuation operations, with the injured transferred to multiple hospitals in Giza and nearby Beni Suef governorate. Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar ordered health facilities in both governorates to raise readiness and provide all necessary medical and emergency support to the injured, according to the statement. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi said on the social media platform Facebook that he was closely following developments, extended his condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Sisi said he had directed state agencies to provide medical care, swiftly investigate the accident and hold anyone found responsible for negligence accountable. The Egyptian National Railways Authority said in an earlier statement that the accident occurred between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations when a train on the Giza-Fayoum route hit the rear of another on the Cairo-Aswan route. Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to clear the site and move the remaining carriages to restore services in both directions as quickly as possible, the authority said. Egypt's railway network has long faced problems of outdated equipment and poor management, leading to frequent accidents. The country's deadliest rail disaster occurred in 2002, when a fire on a Cairo-Luxor train in Giza's Ayyat district killed over 380 people.

items.title: Polémique après son passage au Zénith de Paris : « je suis une Guinéenne », Djélykaba Bintou
items.description: Au lendemain de son passage très réussi sur la scène du Zénith de Paris – La Villette, la chanteuse guinéenne Djélykaba Bintou Kouyaté est revenue sur la polémique suscitée par certaines de ses déclarations. Dans un direct sur TikTok, l’artiste a répondu à ceux qui l’accusent d’avoir rabaissé certaines langues nationales. Face aux critiques sur les réseaux sociaux, Djélykaba Bintou, la fille de Fria, a tenu à rappeler ses origines peules, évoquant notamment sa grand-mère Nènè Issa Barry. « Je vois, y a d’autres qui disent : ah, elle a rabaissé les Peulhs, elle a rabaissé tant, vous ne savez pas que moi, je suis Peule ? Moi, je suis Peule. Humilité à part, si vous voyez comme ça (elle montre son visage), c’est pas femme peule qui est devant vous comme ça ? Si vous voyez une beauté comme ça, une bombe comme ça, ce n’est pas une femme peule qui est devant vous comme ça ? Les Peuls ne vont jamais se fâcher contre moi. Moi, je suis une femme purement peule. Déjà, je suis Djélykaba Bintou Diallo à cause de mon frère Diallo du patronat des États-Unis. Comme vous savez, rien qu’à cause de ma grand-mère Nènè Issa Barry, je suis peule d’une partie. Moi, je suis peule, je suis Maninka, je suis Soussou, je suis Konianké, je suis Guerzé, je suis Landouma, je suis tout, je suis guinéenne », déclare la diva guinéenne, l’artiste la plus en vogue du moment en Guinée. Dans la même intervention, l’artiste a également évoqué la place des langues nationales dans le rayonnement culturel de la Guinée. Revenant sur son passage au Zénith de Paris, elle a expliqué que voir le Sénégal et le Mali porter leurs drapeaux respectifs lui donnait davantage envie de faire rayonner son pays et ses langues. « Quand je vois le Sénégal porter le drapeau du Sénégal, le Mali porter le drapeau du Mali, façon ça me donne envie de porter le drapeau de mon pays comme on l’a fait hier (au Zénith de Paris), tellement que j’ai envie de porter mon pays à la hauteur, tellement que moi aussi j’ai envie d’imposer les langues de la Guinée. Vous n’avez pas compris mais c’est normal. Après un événement, tout ne peut pas être parfait. » À rappeler que, sur scène, l’artiste avait déclaré être Maninka. Ajoutant que le Maninka est une langue universelle, tandis que le Soussou, le Konianké et le Poular ne sont parlés qu’en Guinée. « Donc, on va chanter dans toutes ces langues pour que le monde entier apprenne à chanter dans ces langues grâce à nous, les artistes de Guinée. » Ousmane CAMARA L’article Polémique après son passage au Zénith de Paris : « je suis une Guinéenne », Djélykaba Bintou est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
